docs.title: Where Detectors Apply
docs.text:
Detectors and block policies apply to sync and async clients alike, to the OpenAI Responses API as well as Chat Completions, to all four AWS Bedrock runtime calls (converse, converse_stream, invoke_model, invoke_model_with_response_stream, including the system prompt), and to streamed requests, which are checked before they are sent. A blocked request raises PolicyViolationError before anything reaches the provider, whether or not its trace is sampled.

Framework-level spans (LangChain, LlamaIndex and agent frameworks) are not checked themselves. Detection happens on the provider call beneath them, so the provider's instrumentor has to be enabled for a block policy to take effect. input passed to an embeddings call is not treated as a prompt.

Not covered yet: a prompt passed positionally (LiteLLM, llama.cpp), and providers whose prompt is not messages, prompt or the Responses input: Google Gemini and Vertex AI (contents), Cohere chat (message) and Replicate (input). A block policy does not stop those requests.

docs.title: Where Detectors Run
docs.text:
A block policy is checked before the request is sent, and the call waits for the verdict. On async clients that check runs on a worker thread, so it does not hold your event loop.

The detectors that annotate a span run after your call has returned, on a worker thread. The span is exported when they have finished, with the end time of your call, so its duration is the call's and not the detectors'. Two things follow from that:

  • evaluation.* attributes are not on the span at the moment the call returns. Code that reads them in the same process waits first:

    genai_otel.flush_telemetry()  # waits for pending evaluations, then flushes

  • An LLM span can be exported after the span that encloses it.

To have the detectors finish before the call returns, as they did up to 1.35.0:

genai_otel.instrument(enable_pii_detection=True, evaluation_mode="inline")

or set GENAI_EVALUATION_MODE=inline. Mistral, Hyperbolic, HuggingFace pipelines and Pydantic AI always evaluate inline. A streamed response is evaluated when its stream ends, on the thread that ends it, and only when content capture is on.

If your application installs its own tracer provider before calling instrument(), the detectors run inline and a warning says so: a provider this library did not create does not wait for spans that are still being evaluated when it is flushed or shut down.

docs.title: When Detectors Fall Behind
docs.text:
At most GENAI_EVALUATION_QUEUE_SIZE spans wait for detectors. Past that a span is exported at once without evaluation, marked evaluation.skipped="overloaded", and a warning, at most one a minute, says how many were skipped. Tracing is never slowed or dropped because detectors are slow. Filter on evaluation.skipped to see how much went unevaluated.

Detectors share the Python interpreter with your application. A process that spends its time in Python code, as opposed to waiting on the network, leaves them less time.

docs.title: At Shutdown
docs.text: At exit and on uninstrument(), pending evaluations get GENAI_EVALUATION_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT seconds. Spans the detectors have not reached by then are exported without evaluation, marked evaluation.skipped="shutdown", so no span is lost. In a serverless function, call genai_otel.flush_telemetry() before returning, or use inline mode.

docs.title: How Much Text Is Analysed
docs.text:
Detectors read the last GENAI_EVALUATION_MAX_CHARS characters of a prompt, which is the newest content of a conversation, and the first of a response. The default is 1500. A span whose text was longer says so:

Attribute Meaning evaluation.truncated true when detectors read only part of the text evaluation.prompt.length Characters in the prompt evaluation.prompt.analyzed_length Characters of the prompt the detectors read evaluation.response.length Characters in the response evaluation.response.analyzed_length Characters of the response the detectors read evaluation.pii.prompt.pattern_analyzed_length Characters the PII patterns covered evaluation.pii.prompt.model_analyzed_length Characters the PII entity model read evaluation.<detector>.prompt.analyzed_length Characters a pattern-based detector with a block policy read: the whole prompt

PII detection keeps pattern coverage of the whole prompt. Card numbers, e-mail addresses, phone numbers, US social security numbers, IP addresses, the Indian identifiers and your custom patterns are found wherever they are. Entity types that need the language model, such as names and locations, are looked for only in the analysed part.

The local toxicity model has its own, smaller limit: it reads the last GENAI_TOXICITY_MAX_CHARS characters of the prompt (default 500), recorded in evaluation.toxicity.prompt.analyzed_length. With both limits at 0 it scores the whole text in pieces and reports the highest score per category.

PII in redact mode is not limited: a redacted copy is only built from text that was analysed. Under GENAI_PROFILE=strict both limits default to 0.

A block policy on prompt injection, restricted topics or bias always reads the whole prompt, whatever the limit, so padding a prompt cannot hide text from it. The span records that in evaluation.<detector>.prompt.analyzed_length.

The limit applies to PII and toxicity block policies

With a block policy, text outside the analysed part is not checked for toxicity, and not for names or locations. Set GENAI_EVALUATION_MAX_CHARS=0 and GENAI_TOXICITY_MAX_CHARS=0 when every character must be checked. Detection time then grows with the length of the prompt.

With a block policy a prompt is analysed once per call: the check before the request and the annotation after it share the result. Each detector remembers its most recent results, keyed by a digest of the analysed text and never by the text itself (GENAI_EVALUATION_CACHE_SIZE).

docs.title: Toxicity Model Options
docs.text:
GENAI_TOXICITY_QUANTIZE=true runs the local Detoxify model with 8-bit weights. It is faster, and its scores differ from the default model's by enough to change some verdicts near the threshold, so compare the two on your own data before relying on it. It is off by default.

GENAI_TOXICITY_TORCH_THREADS sets how many threads torch may use. The setting is process-wide and applies to every torch model in the process, so it is unset by default.

Enabling only the pattern-based detectors (bias, prompt injection, restricted topics, hallucination) does not load torch or the toxicity model.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Each detector records metrics for monitoring:

  • genai.evaluation.<detector>.detections - Detection events
  • genai.evaluation.<detector>.blocked - Blocked requests
  • genai.evaluation.<detector>.score - Score distribution (histogram)

See the README for the complete list of span attributes.

docs.title: Evaluation outcomes, provenance, and coverage
docs.text:
Evaluation spans carry bounded outcome metadata so a missing verdict cannot be read as a successful check:

Attribute Values / meaning evaluation.outcome completed, no_applicable_input, unsupported_operation, skipped, or error for the detector suite evaluation.<detector>.outcome The same bounded values for pii, toxicity, bias, prompt_injection, restricted_topics, and hallucination evaluation.content.outcomes A bounded list containing captured, omitted, truncated, redacted, rejected, or error as applicable evaluation.provenance.sdk.name / .version SDK identity and installed version evaluation.provenance.detector.<name>.implementation / .version Detector implementation identifier and SDK version evaluation.config.fingerprint SHA-256 of a normalized schema version and the enabled detector names; thresholds, custom values, credentials, and content are excluded

completed means that the detector ran on at least one applicable text input. It is not a claim that every part of the operation was captured, that detection is complete, or that a policy was enforced. no_applicable_input means the instrumentor did not provide usable text; unsupported_operation identifies operations such as embeddings, for which these text detectors do not apply; skipped records work bypassed by queue pressure or shutdown; and error records a detector failure. These attributes are additive and do not change detection, redaction, blocking, or content-capture behavior.

docs.title: Operation surfaces
docs.text:
The evaluation processor reads text supplied through GenAI prompt events (gen_ai.prompt.*), prompt attributes (gen_ai.prompt, gen_ai.request.prompt, gen_ai.request.first_message), OpenInference llm.input_messages / llm.output_messages, and common input.value / output.value attributes. It analyzes text that the SDK instrumentor can extract as a string. Input checks cover prompts; PII, toxicity, bias, and restricted-topic checks can also cover response text; prompt-injection checks cover prompts; hallucination checks cover responses.

Streaming checks run after a supported stream finishes and its instrumentor has assembled text. A stream that is abandoned, closed before text is available, or whose instrumentor does not expose text may have no applicable input or be skipped. Embedding vectors, image/audio payloads, and other non-text content are not evaluated by these detectors. Only content actually present on the span can be reported as captured; no outcome field contains source text. The reported outcome is instrumentation evidence, not proof of complete capture or runtime enforcement. Blocking is enforced only by the separate pre-call policy hook.

docs.title: GPU Metrics and CO2 Tracking
docs.text: TraceVerde collects real-time GPU metrics for both NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, with optional CO2 emissions and electricity cost tracking.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
# NVIDIA GPUs
pip install genai-otel-instrument[gpu]

# AMD GPUs
pip install genai-otel-instrument[amd-gpu]

# Both
pip install genai-otel-instrument[all-gpu]

# CO2 tracking (adds codecarbon)
pip install genai-otel-instrument[co2]

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Variable Default Description GENAI_ENABLE_GPU_METRICS true Enable GPU metrics collection GENAI_GPU_COLLECTION_INTERVAL 5 Collection interval in seconds GENAI_POWER_COST_PER_KWH 0.12 Electricity cost in USD per kWh

Common electricity rates: - US average: ~$0.12/kWh - Europe average: ~$0.20/kWh - Industrial/datacenter: ~$0.07/kWh

The collector runs in a background daemon thread and gracefully handles systems without GPUs.

docs.title: CO2 Emissions Tracking
docs.text: Track the carbon footprint of your GPU workloads. Two calculation modes are available:

docs.title: Codecarbon Mode (Recommended)
docs.text:
Uses codecarbon for automatic region-specific carbon intensity lookup.

pip install genai-otel-instrument[co2]

import genai_otel

genai_otel.instrument(
    enable_co2_tracking=True,
    co2_country_iso_code="USA",    # 3-letter ISO code
    co2_region="california",       # Optional: state/region
)

Or for cloud environments:

genai_otel.instrument(
    enable_co2_tracking=True,
    co2_cloud_provider="aws",
    co2_cloud_region="us-east-1",
)

docs.title: Manual Mode
docs.text:
Use a fixed carbon intensity value without codecarbon:

genai_otel.instrument(
    enable_co2_tracking=True,
    co2_use_manual=True,
    carbon_intensity=56.0,  # gCO2e/kWh (France - mostly nuclear)
)

Reference carbon intensity values (gCO2e/kWh):

Country/Region gCO2e/kWh Notes France ~56 Mostly nuclear Sweden ~13 Mostly hydro/wind UK ~233 Mix Germany ~350 Mix with coal US average ~420 Varies by state US (California) ~210 Renewables-heavy US (West Virginia) ~860 Coal-heavy China ~555 Coal-heavy India ~700 Coal-heavy

docs.title: Example: Full GPU + CO2 Setup
docs.text:
export GENAI_ENABLE_GPU_METRICS=true
export GENAI_GPU_COLLECTION_INTERVAL=10
export GENAI_ENABLE_CO2_TRACKING=true
export GENAI_CO2_COUNTRY_ISO_CODE=USA
export GENAI_CO2_REGION=california
export GENAI_POWER_COST_PER_KWH=0.18

import genai_otel

genai_otel.instrument(
    service_name="gpu-workload",
    enable_gpu_metrics=True,
    gpu_collection_interval=10,
    enable_co2_tracking=True,
    co2_country_iso_code="USA",
    co2_region="california",
    power_cost_per_kwh=0.18,
)

# Run your GPU workload
import transformers
pipe = transformers.pipeline("text-generation", model="gpt2", device=0)
result = pipe("Hello world", max_length=50)

# GPU metrics, CO2 emissions, and electricity costs are all tracked automatically

docs.title: xAI SDK
docs.text:
Install the optional SDK dependency and set your xAI API key as XAI_API_KEY:

pip install "genai-otel-instrument[xai]"

Enable xai_sdk before creating the xAI client. Chat sample() and stream(), image generation, and video generation are traced for both Client and AsyncClient, including model, usage, latency, and xAI's exact reported request cost. The xAI Text to Speech REST endpoint is also traced; cost uses the published per-character rate because its audio response does not include a cost field. STT REST calls are priced when the response provides audio duration. Request text and audio are not captured. See the chat, image/video, and voice examples.

The current official Python package exposes chat, image, and video helpers. Voice helpers are not part of its released Client API yet, so TTS and STT are currently instrumented through the documented xAI REST endpoints. WebSocket voice sessions are not covered by this integration.

import genai_otel
from xai_sdk import Client
from xai_sdk.chat import user

genai_otel.instrument(enabled_instrumentors=["xai_sdk"])
client = Client()
chat = client.chat.create(model="grok-4.6")
chat.append(user("Hello"))
response = chat.sample()
print(response.content)

xAI also offers an opt-in telemetry exporter in its SDK. Configure one exporter path at a time to avoid duplicate spans for the same SDK calls.

docs.title: Databricks Model Serving
docs.text:
Install the integration and OpenAI-compatible SDK:

pip install "genai-otel-instrument[databricks]"

Enable the Databricks instrumentor before creating the client. Point it at a Databricks workspace serving endpoint and pass the endpoint or model-service name in model. Credentials stay in environment variables:

import os

import genai_otel
from openai import OpenAI

genai_otel.instrument(enabled_instrumentors=["databricks"])

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.environ["DATABRICKS_TOKEN"],
    base_url=f"{os.environ['DATABRICKS_HOST'].rstrip('/')}/serving-endpoints",
)
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model=os.environ["DATABRICKS_MODEL"],
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello from TraceVerde"}],
)

Set DATABRICKS_HOST to your workspace URL, DATABRICKS_TOKEN to a token with query access, and DATABRICKS_MODEL to the serving endpoint name. The instrumentor also recognizes Databricks AI Gateway routes under /ai-gateway/ and works with databricks-openai clients that use these endpoints. It records chat, completions, embeddings, and Responses API calls as databricks.* spans with gen_ai.provider.name=databricks. See the complete Databricks example.

The native Databricks SDK is supported too:

import genai_otel
from databricks.sdk import WorkspaceClient
from databricks.sdk.service.serving import ChatMessage, ChatMessageRole

genai_otel.instrument(enabled_instrumentors=["databricks"])
workspace = WorkspaceClient()  # Uses Databricks SDK authentication configuration
result = workspace.serving_endpoints.query(
    name="my-chat-endpoint",
    messages=[ChatMessage(role=ChatMessageRole.USER, content="Hello")],
)
See the complete native SDK example.

MLflow deployment clients are supported as well. The [databricks] extra includes mlflow-skinny for this path. Calls to predict and predict_stream on get_deploy_client("databricks") are recorded as Databricks spans; streaming spans stay open through iteration so final-chunk token usage is captured. Other MLflow deployment targets are left to their own provider instrumentation.

import genai_otel
from mlflow.deployments import get_deploy_client

genai_otel.instrument(enabled_instrumentors=["databricks"])
client = get_deploy_client("databricks")
response = client.predict(
    endpoint="my-chat-endpoint",
    inputs={"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]},
)

See the MLflow example. ChatDatabricks from databricks-langchain is also covered when its underlying client uses a Databricks serving-endpoint or AI Gateway URL; the Databricks client span is emitted under any framework span produced by LangChain.

docs.title: Decision models
docs.text: A decision model takes a state plus a set of typed questions and returns, for each question, a probability distribution over answers you supplied. It writes no text. TraceVerde records every decision-model call as an OpenInference DECISION span (openinference.span.kind = DECISION), whichever way it was made, with one attribute shape and its own cost.

docs.title: Protocols and call paths
docs.text:
Almost every decision model speaks one of two wire protocols, so the library instruments call paths, not models. A Hub decision model served through any of these paths is covered without an instrumentor of its own.

Call path Protocol Span Covers client.decisions.create (OpenAI SDK, sync and async, with_raw_response too) OpenAI Decisions (POST /v1/decisions) openai.decisions OpenAI gpt-6-luna; Azure OpenAI through AzureOpenAI; OpenRouter (openrouter.decisions); any server that answers /v1/decisions client.decisions.create / client.aio.decisions.create (google-genai 3.2+, api_version="v1beta") Gemini Decisions (POST /v1beta/decisions) google.genai.decisions / google.genai.aio.decisions Google gemini-decision-1. Per-modality input tokens land in decision.token_count.input.<modality>; a safety 400 is an ERROR span with error.type set to the API's error.code. No-op on a google-genai without decisions TypeSafeClient.system_one / AsyncTypeSafeClient.system_one (typesafe-sdk, any base_url) SystemOne (POST /v1/systemone) typesafe.system_one TypeSafe Jev, LiquidAI D1 / D1 Ultra, Cloudflare Workers AI, vLLM / SGLang / Ollajev / laya-serve serving Hub decision models (JEV, Clef, GEV, decider, ...) a POST with requests, httpx or httpx2 to .../v1/systemone, .../decisions/v1/systemone, .../v1/decisions, or https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/decisions (matched on that host only), outside an SDK call any of the three decision.http.systemone / decision.http.openai / decision.http.google apps that call the endpoints without an SDK, such as LiquidAI's image examples OpenAI chat completions with extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"adapter_name": "decision"}} Granite Switch decision adapter openai.chat.decision IBM Granite Switch 4.1 on vLLM. Its other adapters (guardian-core) stay chat spans genai_otel.decision_span (context manager or decorator) in-process decision (or your name) Laya Router, Clef's joint_schema_model.systemone, transformers checkpoints, rules engines

GENAI_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTORS=openai covers OpenAI Decisions and Granite Switch; typesafe covers SystemOne. The HTTP path matcher is governed by GENAI_DECISION_HTTP_MATCHER (on by default) and never wraps a call already inside an SDK decision span, so one decision is one span. An openai release without the Decisions resource (before 3.26) is skipped silently.

LLM structured outputs, logprob classification on a plain chat model and Instructor still produce generated text that is parsed, so they stay LLM spans. To record one of them as a decision, use decision_span.

docs.title: Self-hosted servers
docs.text:
Point the client at your server:

from typesafe_sdk import TypeSafeClient

client = TypeSafeClient(api_key="unused", base_url="http://localhost:8000")  # vLLM / SGLang
client.system_one(state=ticket, questions=questions, model="Cloudflare/clef-flash")

decision.provider is taken from the host: api.openai.com -> openai, openrouter.ai -> openrouter, api.liquid.ai -> liquid, api.typesafe.ai -> typesafe, api.cloudflare.com -> cloudflare, *.openai.azure.com -> azure. Any other host is self-hosted and gets no provider, unless GENAI_DECISION_PROVIDER names one.

docs.title: In-process models
docs.text:
from genai_otel import decision_span

with decision_span(model="laya-router-421m", questions=questions, state=message) as d:
    result = router(message)
    d.record({"next_tool": {"type": "choice", "choice": result.label,
                            "confidence": result.confidence,
                            "probabilities": result.probabilities}},
             usage=None)   # leave usage out when the model reports none

questions and answers may be a SystemOne mapping or an OpenAI Decisions list. As a decorator, the function's return value is recorded when it is a response (has answers) or a set of answers. d.fail(message) ends the span as an error without an exception.

A decision over audio passes it as audio= (bytes, a path, a binary file object or a (name, file) tuple), with audio_format= when the format cannot be told from the bytes or the file name:

with decision_span(model="eot-detector", questions=questions, audio=clip_wav) as d:
    d.record({"finished": {"type": "noul", "probability": model(clip_wav)}})

docs.title: Audio and image inputs
docs.text:
Decision requests can carry images and audio: input_image / input_audio parts, data URLs, asset objects, raw bytes and decision_span(audio=...). They are recognised by part type, then MIME type, then the first bytes (WAV, MP3, OGG, FLAC, WebM; PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP). Bytes of no known kind are [binary omitted], never called an image.

  • genai.decision.input.modalities (text, image, audio) is recorded on every DECISION span, with content capture off too: it says what kind of input was decided on, not what it said.
  • genai.decision.input.audio_seconds is recorded when the audio is WAV, whose duration the header gives without decoding.
  • With media capture on (GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_CAPTURE_MODE), each image and audio input becomes a media part (gen_ai.prompt.0.content.<m>.*) through the same size cap, modality allow-list, redactor and store as every other media part. With content capture on as well, input.value refers to the stored copy ([audio: <uri>]) instead of the placeholder.

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute When Notes openinference.span.kind = DECISION always LLM on SystemOne calls under GENAI_DECISION_LEGACY_LLM_KIND=true decision.system always the API shape: openai, typesafe, or custom for the helper decision.provider recognised host, or GENAI_DECISION_PROVIDER never guessed decision.model_name always response model, else request model decision.request.model_name, decision.response.model_name when they differ decision.token_count.input, .output only when the provider reports them never 0 for a missing value gen_ai.system, gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.response.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens, gen_ai.usage.output_tokens always / when reported kept so gen_ai.* readers see decisions gen_ai.operation.name always openai.decisions, typesafe.system_one, openai.chat.decision or decision gen_ai.request.type = decision always selects the decision pricing section gen_ai.usage.cost.total, gen_ai.usage.cost.decision when the model is priced the same value on both genai.decision.protocol always openai_decisions, systemone, granite_adapter or manual genai.decision.question_count, .refusal_count, .question.types always counts and types only (predicate, choice, score, refusal, box; SystemOne's noul is recorded as predicate) genai.decision.option_count one-question calls how many choices or levels were offered genai.decision.question.names content capture on caller labels can be sensitive genai.decision.min_confidence content capture on lowest confidence across choice and score answers genai.decision.choice, .confidence, .probability, .score, .margin content capture on, one-question calls margin is the top probability minus the second genai.decision.input.modalities always text, image, audio: what the input carried genai.decision.input.audio_seconds WAV audio inputs from the header input.value, output.value, *.mime_type = application/json content capture on the request and response JSON with media replaced by [image omitted], [audio omitted] or [binary omitted] (or [<kind>: <uri>] when media capture stored it), capped at GENAI_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH

SystemOne spans also keep the attributes they carried as LLM spans before 1.38 (llm.request.model_name, llm.response.model_name, llm.token_count.*, llm.invocation_parameters, gen_ai.response) until 2.0.

docs.title: What content capture decides
docs.text: With content capture off (the default) a decision span says which model decided, through which provider, how many questions of which types, how many were refused, tokens, cost, latency and status, and nothing about the answer: no chosen value, no confidence or score, no question names, no state. GENAI_ENABLE_CONTENT_CAPTURE=true adds them. The default 200-character content cap truncates the request and response JSON, which is why the summary attributes exist.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text:
Decision models are priced from their own decision section of the pricing table, and only from it. A model missing from that section gets no cost attribute rather than a chat price: gpt-6-luna used as a decision model bills input only, while gpt-6-luna the chat model bills output at $0.50/1M.

Model key Input per 1M Output gpt-6-luna (OpenAI Decisions; cache reads and writes free) $0.10 $0 openai/gpt-6-luna-decisions (OpenRouter) $0.10 $0 gemini-decision-1 (Google Gemini Decisions) $0.10 $0 d1 / d1-ultra (LiquidAI, any route) $0.02 / $0.042 $0 jev (TypeSafe) $0.042 $0 clef, clef-flash, clef-omni not priced until Cloudflare publishes a price

Dated and routed variants resolve to their key (jev-1.13.0-20260917, liquid/d1). Self-hosted weights (Hub models, Granite Switch, Laya) have no list price and get no cost attribute; price one with a decision section in GENAI_CUSTOM_PRICING_JSON. Regional and long-context multipliers are not modelled.

docs.title: Evaluation
docs.text: On decision spans the input is still screened for PII, prompt injection and restricted topics. Hallucination and response checks are skipped, because there is no generated text, and the span says so with evaluation.skipped_reason = decision_span.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: examples/decisions/ has one runnable example per call path; the README there says which ones need a key or a server.

docs.title: Fast/slow routing
docs.text:
A common agent pattern: a small decision model handles most steps, and a router sends a step to a large model only when it judges the step needs it. Two things show whether that pays off.

Why the router chose the model. Routers return their choice in response headers, and which headers depends on the router. List the ones to record:

GENAI_CAPTURE_RESPONSE_HEADERS=x-litellm-model-id,x-litellm-model-group,x-litellm-attempted-fallbacks

instrument(capture_response_headers=[...]) does the same, and GENAI_ROUTER_RESPONSE_HEADERS is accepted as another name. Each listed header goes on the model-call span as http.response.header.<name>, a string array. Nothing is recorded by default. Credential headers (authorization, cookie, set-cookie, x-api-key, api-key and any name containing auth, secret, password or cookie) are never recorded, even when listed. This applies to OpenAI-compatible clients (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, a LiteLLM proxy or any base_url), sync and async, plain and with_raw_response.

When a router answers with another model than the one requested (model="auto" served by gpt-5.5), the span says so: gen_ai.router.requested_model is the alias, next to gen_ai.response.model. A dated snapshot of the requested model does not count.

Which decision caused which call. Link the model calls a decision causes to it:

from genai_otel import decision_span, escalation_from

with decision_span(model="router-421m", questions=questions, state=step) as d:
    d.record(router(step))

if needs_large_model:
    with escalation_from(d):
        client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-5.5", messages=messages)

Every model call (chat, completions, Responses, embeddings, speech) started inside the block gets an OpenTelemetry span link to the decision. Agent, tool and HTTP spans do not, so a call is not counted twice. The link does not change the call's parent. For a decision made through an SDK (client.decisions.create), use escalation_from(genai_otel.last_decision()).

With GENAI_LINK_DECISIONS=true, the next model call after a decision in the same context is linked automatically, marked inferred. Concurrent asyncio tasks never link to each other's decisions. Tasks started after a decision share it, and the first call among them takes it.

Each link is mirrored as genai.decision.link.span_id and genai.decision.link.inferred on the linked span, since some trace stores keep a link's ids but not its attributes.

docs.title: TypeSafe AI / Jev
docs.text:
TypeSafe's System One API evaluates typed questions against unstructured state and returns decisions instead of generated prose. TraceVerde wraps both TypeSafeClient.system_one and AsyncTypeSafeClient.system_one natively, as DECISION spans (see Decision models): the model, the provider behind base_url, question counts and types, token usage and Jev's published input price, and, with content capture on, the typed answers and their confidence.

Before 1.38 these were LLM spans. The llm.* attributes are still emitted until 2.0, and GENAI_DECISION_LEGACY_LLM_KIND=true keeps the old span kind.

pip install 'genai-otel-instrument[typesafe]'
export TYPESAFE_API_KEY="your-key"
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT="https://otel.example.internal:4318"
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL="http/protobuf"
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATE="/absolute/path/to/platform-ca.crt"
export GENAI_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTORS="typesafe"
export GENAI_ENABLE_CONTENT_CAPTURE=true
export GENAI_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH=0
python examples/typesafe/example.py

The example sends one state with a Choice, Noul, and Score question so you can inspect the complete structured response in the terminal and the resulting typesafe.system_one span in the platform backend. The OTLP endpoint must use HTTPS, and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATE must point to the CA certificate that signed it.

Replicate hosts arbitrary community models behind one generic run() call, with no fixed input/output schema and no dedicated embeddings endpoint to hook. Embedding calls are recognized by matching the model reference against known embedding-only model families (BGE, E5, GTE, MPNet, MiniLM, and any model whose name contains "embed"); a model outside those families is traced as a plain replicate.run span, cost tracking excluded, same as before.

docs.title: Audio Providers: Billing by Media, Not Tokens
docs.text:
ElevenLabs is billed per unit of media rather than per token, so its spans carry different usage attributes. Text-to-speech is priced per character of input text and Scribe speech-to-text per second of audio.

import genai_otel
genai_otel.instrument()

from elevenlabs import ElevenLabs
client = ElevenLabs(api_key="...")

# Text-to-speech: convert() returns an iterator of audio bytes. Draining it is
# what completes the span and records time-to-first-byte.
audio = b"".join(client.text_to_speech.convert(
    voice_id="21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM",
    text="Hello from TraceVerde.",
    model_id="eleven_multilingual_v2",
))

# Scribe speech-to-text
transcript = client.speech_to_text.convert(model_id="scribe_v1", file=open("call.mp3", "rb"))
Attribute Operation Meaning gen_ai.usage.characters text_to_speech Input characters, the billed unit gen_ai.server.time_to_first_token text_to_speech Time to first audio byte (also emitted as gen_ai.server.ttft) gen_ai.request.voice_id text_to_speech Voice used for synthesis gen_ai.usage.audio_duration_seconds speech_to_text Audio seconds, the billed unit gen_ai.response.transcript_length speech_to_text Characters of transcript returned

Time-to-first-byte matters more than total duration for voice, since streamed synthesis begins playing before generation finishes - it is what the caller actually waits for on a voice turn.

Audio payloads are never attached to spans. Only sizes and durations are recorded. For voice workloads the audio is frequently personal data, so reference-only is the default rather than something to opt into.

docs.title: OpenAI speech: transcriptions, translations and text-to-speech
docs.text:
client.audio.transcriptions.create, client.audio.translations.create and client.audio.speech.create are traced on OpenAI, AsyncOpenAI and AzureOpenAI clients, including their with_raw_response and with_streaming_response variants and streamed transcription (stream=True). The spans are openai.audio.transcriptions, openai.audio.translations and openai.audio.speech, with the attributes in the table above. A translation also carries gen_ai.request.target_language_code=en: OpenAI translates only into English.

Cost comes from what OpenAI bills:

Model Billed by Read from whisper-1 seconds of audio the response's usage.seconds or duration; for text/srt/vtt responses, the WAV header of the upload gpt-4o-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize input and output tokens, at separate rates the response's usage tts-1, tts-1-hd characters of input the request gpt-4o-mini-tts input and output tokens, at separate rates only stream_format="sse" responses report usage

When the billed quantity is not knowable (gpt-4o-mini-tts without sse, a whisper-1 text response on non-WAV audio), the span has no cost and gen_ai.usage.cost.unknown_reason says why (no_usage_reported, or unpriced_model for an Azure deployment name with no price). A plausible wrong cost is worse than none.

A speech span stays open until its audio has been read. Streamed speech records the time to the first audio chunk. Speech the caller stops reading early ends with genai.stream.closed_early=true and is still billed for its characters.

With media capture on (GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_CAPTURE_MODE), the uploaded audio and the synthesised audio are recorded as media parts, through the media pipeline's size cap, allow-list and redactor. With content capture on, the transcript and the input text are recorded. Both are off by default. The upload is read before the SDK sends it, and a file object is returned to where it was.

docs.title: Quick Example: Responses API
docs.text:
client.responses.create is traced as its own span (openai.responses). This is the default path for native GPT-5.6+ models, because Chat Completions rejects function tools combined with reasoning -- so agent runtimes that use tools and reasoning together end up here rather than on chat.completions.create.

import genai_otel
genai_otel.instrument()

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()
response = client.responses.create(
    model="gpt-5.6",
    instructions="You are a helpful assistant.",
    input="What is OpenTelemetry?",
    max_output_tokens=150,
)

print(response.output_text)

The Responses shape differs from Chat Completions in every field the instrumentation reads, and each is mapped onto the same semantic conventions so Responses and Chat Completions spans stay comparable:

Responses Chat Completions Recorded as input (string or list), instructions messages gen_ai.request.message_count, gen_ai.request.first_message, gen_ai.request.instructions max_output_tokens max_tokens gen_ai.request.max_tokens output[] items choices[] completion events, gen_ai.response usage.input_tokens / output_tokens usage.prompt_tokens / completion_tokens gen_ai.usage.input_tokens / gen_ai.usage.output_tokens output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens gen_ai.usage.reasoning_tokens input_tokens_details.cached_tokens prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens status / incomplete_details.reason choices[].finish_reason gen_ai.response.finish_reasons

Reasoning tokens are attributed as output, because that is how they are billed. Tool calls come from the function_call items of output[], and response.id is recorded so store=true responses stay joinable server-side. Streaming works the same as elsewhere -- TTFT and inter-token latency are measured as the response events arrive.

docs.title: Quick Example: AWS Bedrock Converse
docs.text:
All four Bedrock runtime calls are traced: invoke_model, invoke_model_with_response_stream, converse and converse_stream.

Converse is the unified API AWS points callers at, and the practical path for every non-Anthropic model -- it removes the per-vendor request body that makes invoke_model awkward. Because it is model-agnostic, the span shape does not depend on modelId.

import genai_otel
genai_otel.instrument()

import boto3

client = boto3.client("bedrock-runtime", region_name="us-east-1")
response = client.converse(
    modelId="meta.llama3-70b-instruct-v1:0",
    system=[{"text": "You are a helpful assistant."}],
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": [{"text": "What is OpenTelemetry?"}]}],
    inferenceConfig={"maxTokens": 256, "temperature": 0.2},
)

print(response["output"]["message"]["content"][0]["text"])

Converse differs from invoke_model in every field the instrumentation reads, and each is mapped onto the same semantic conventions the other providers emit:

Converse Recorded as modelId gen_ai.request.model messages[].content[] typed blocks (text, image, toolUse, toolResult) gen_ai.request.message_count, gen_ai.request.first_message system (a top-level parameter, not a message role) gen_ai.request.instructions inferenceConfig.{maxTokens, temperature, topP, stopSequences} gen_ai.request.{max_tokens, temperature, top_p, stop_sequences} output.message.content[] completion events, gen_ai.response usage.{inputTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens} (camelCase) gen_ai.usage.{input_tokens, output_tokens} stopReason gen_ai.response.finish_reasons toolUse blocks tool-call attributes

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
converse_stream returns {"stream": ...} immediately -- the model generates while you iterate -- so the span stays open until the event stream is exhausted rather than closing on return, which would report near-zero latency and no tokens. Token counts arrive only in the trailing metadata event and are picked up from there.

response = client.converse_stream(
    modelId="meta.llama3-70b-instruct-v1:0",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Explain tracing."}]}],
)

for event in response["stream"]:
    if "contentBlockDelta" in event:
        print(event["contentBlockDelta"]["delta"]["text"], end="")

docs.title: Quick Example: Embeddings and RAG
docs.text:
Embedding calls are traced as their own spans, so a retrieval-augmented call shows both of its legs: the lookup that chose the context and the generation that used it. Without the embedding span, the retrieval step is invisible and its tokens and cost go unrecorded.

import genai_otel
genai_otel.instrument()

from openai import OpenAI
from opentelemetry import trace

client = OpenAI()
tracer = trace.get_tracer("rag.demo")

with tracer.start_as_current_span("rag.pipeline"):
    # 1. Index - one span, input_count = number of chunks
    indexed = client.embeddings.create(
        model="text-embedding-3-small",
        input=["chunk one", "chunk two", "chunk three"],
    )

    # 2. Retrieve - one span for the query embedding
    query = client.embeddings.create(
        model="text-embedding-3-small",
        input="what did chunk two say?",
    )

    # 3. Generate - the chat span, as usual
    client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o-mini",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Answer from the retrieved context."}],
    )

Wrapping the three calls in a parent span groups them into a single trace, so the whole pipeline is one unit in the UI rather than three unrelated calls.

Embedding spans carry gen_ai.request.input_count, gen_ai.response.embedding_count and gen_ai.response.vector_size alongside the usual token and cost attributes, priced against the embeddings table. The embedded text itself is recorded as embedding.text only when GENAI_ENABLE_CONTENT_CAPTURE=true, since retrieval inputs frequently contain user data. Vectors stay off entirely unless explicitly requested - they would otherwise dominate span size. See the semantic conventions reference for the full attribute list.

docs.title: Quick Example: Anthropic
docs.text:
Anthropic Python SDK 1.14.0 and later emits native OpenTelemetry request spans by default. When those spans are enabled on a client, TraceVerde leaves that client's Messages methods unwrapped, avoiding duplicate request spans while applying its usual cost enrichment to the native GenAI usage attributes. If you set open_telemetry=False on the client (or ANTHROPIC_OPEN_TELEMETRY=false before client creation), TraceVerde uses its own Messages wrapper instead.

import genai_otel
genai_otel.instrument()

import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()
message = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "Explain quantum computing in one sentence."}
    ],
)

print(message.content[0].text)
# Cost tracking and token usage automatically captured

docs.title: Quick Example: CometAPI
docs.text:
CometAPI is an all-in-one aggregator that exposes 500+ models (GPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, and more) behind a single API key. It is compatible with both the Anthropic SDK and the OpenAI SDK - point either client's base_url at https://api.cometapi.com and TraceVerde detects and traces the calls with gen_ai.system = "cometapi".

import genai_otel
genai_otel.instrument()

import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic(
    base_url="https://api.cometapi.com",
    api_key="your-cometapi-key",  # from https://www.cometapi.com/console/token
)
message = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "Can you describe LLMs to me?"}
    ],
)

print(message.content[0].text)
# Spans named cometapi.messages.create with token usage and cost tracking

The OpenAI SDK works the same way with base_url="https://api.cometapi.com/v1" (spans are named cometapi.chat.completion).

One span per call

Aggregator clients (CometAPI, OpenRouter) are traced only by their dedicated instrumentor - the generic OpenAI/Anthropic instrumentors skip clients whose base_url points at an aggregator, so each call produces exactly one span and one set of token/cost metrics (since v1.5.1). If you disable the aggregator instrumentor, the generic SDK instrumentor traces those clients instead.

    "s3",
    endpoint_url="https://seaweed-s3.example.internal:8333",
    region_name="us-east-1",
    aws_access_key_id=os.environ["AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"],
    aws_secret_access_key=os.environ["AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"],
    config=Config(signature_version="s3v4", s3={"addressing_style": "path"}),
)
s3.put_object(Bucket="agent-artifacts", Key="sessions/output.json", Body=b"{}")
s3.get_object(Bucket="agent-artifacts", Key="sessions/output.json")

Configure the endpoint and credentials for your SeaweedFS deployment. SeaweedFS supports S3 Signature Version 4 and documents its S3 gateway credentials in its S3 API guide. The example uses path-style addressing, which works with a gateway that has not been configured for virtual-hosted bucket domains. Spans record the operation, bucket, object key, and endpoint hostname; they do not record credentials, request bodies, or object contents. For GetObject, the span measures the S3 API request through response creation; later reads from the returned streaming body happen outside it. See the runnable SDK example for direct S3 tracing and the multimodal offload store together.

docs.title: CrewAI
docs.text:
Span hierarchy: Crew -> Task -> Agent -> LLM calls, in one trace per kickoff. For the Arize AX agent graph the crew span is the root node and each agent execution a node beneath it; see Arize AX. Verified against CrewAI 1.15.27 and 1.14.4.

pip install genai-otel-instrument[crewai]

import genai_otel

genai_otel.instrument(
    service_name="my-crewai-app",
    enabled_instrumentors=["crewai", "openai"],
)

from crewai import LLM, Agent, Crew, Process, Task
from crewai.tools import tool


@tool("word_count")
def word_count(text: str) -> str:
    """Count the words in the given text and return the number."""
    return str(len(text.split()))


llm = LLM(model="gpt-4o-mini", max_tokens=80, temperature=0)

counter = Agent(
    role="Word Counter",
    goal="Count words exactly using the word_count tool",
    backstory="A careful clerk who never guesses a count.",
    llm=llm,
    tools=[word_count],
)
reporter = Agent(
    role="Reporter",
    goal="State results in one short sentence",
    backstory="A terse reporter.",
    llm=llm,
)

count_task = Task(
    description="Use the word_count tool on 'OpenTelemetry traces every agent step'.",
    expected_output="The word count as a number.",
    agent=counter,
)
report_task = Task(
    description="Write one sentence stating the word count found.",
    expected_output="One short sentence.",
    agent=reporter,
)

crew = Crew(
    agents=[counter, reporter],
    tasks=[count_task, report_task],
    process=Process.sequential,
)
result = crew.kickoff()
# crewai.crew.execution -> crewai.task.execution -> crewai.agent.execution -> openai.chat.completion

Call genai_otel.instrument() before importing crewai and before creating any LLM or Agent. An OpenAI client built before instrumentation is not traced, and on CrewAI older than 1.15.15 importing crewai first lets CrewAI's own telemetry take the global tracer provider, in which case no TraceVerde span is exported (a warning is logged).

Instrumented methods:

  • Crew.kickoff(), kickoff_async(), akickoff(), kickoff_for_each() and async batch variants
  • Task.execute_sync(), Task.execute_async(), Task.aexecute_sync()
  • Agent.execute_task(), Agent.aexecute_task()

Span types:

  • crewai.crew.execution - crew-level attributes (process type, agent/task counts, output)
  • crewai.task.execution - task attributes (description, expected output, gen_ai.agent.name)
  • crewai.agent.execution - agent attributes (role, goal, backstory, LLM model)

What to expect:

  • Tokens and cost are on the LLM spans. The crew span reports them itself only when no LLM span beneath it did, and then for that kickoff alone. Batch runs that overlap in time (kickoff_for_each_async) share their LLM's counters, so in that case each crew span can include usage from the others.
  • session.id is inputs={"session_id": ...} when you pass one, else the enclosing genai_otel.session() block, else the crew's id. Every task, agent, LLM and tool span of the kickoff carries it.
  • Tool calls have no span of their own; they appear as llm.tools and tool-call attributes on the LLM span.
  • A task with output_pydantic goes through the OpenAI SDK's parse call, which is not traced yet, so it has no LLM span.
  • kickoff_for_each produces one outer crewai.crew.execution span around one per input.
  • TraceVerde sets CREWAI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true so CrewAI's built-in telemetry does not run alongside it. Set the variable yourself to keep your own choice. CREWAI_TRACING_ENABLED=false removes CrewAI's first-run prompt to share a trace.

Includes automatic ThreadPoolExecutor context propagation for worker threads.

See CrewAI example.

docs.title: LangGraph
docs.text:
Stateful workflows with graph-based orchestration. Verified against LangGraph 0.1.19, 0.2.76, 0.6.11 and 1.2.14.

pip install genai-otel-instrument[langgraph]

import genai_otel

genai_otel.instrument(
    service_name="my-langgraph-app",
    enabled_instrumentors=["langgraph", "openai"],
)

from typing import TypedDict

from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph


class State(TypedDict, total=False):
    question: str
    answer: str


llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini", max_tokens=12)


def answer(state: State):
    return {"answer": llm.invoke(state["question"]).content}


builder = StateGraph(State)
builder.add_node("answer", answer)
builder.add_edge(START, "answer")
builder.add_edge("answer", END)
graph = builder.compile()

result = graph.invoke(
    {"question": "Capital of France? One word."},
    {"configurable": {"thread_id": "user-42"}},
)
# langgraph.graph.invoke -> langgraph.node.answer -> openai.chat.completion

How it hooks in. TraceVerde wraps four methods on the langgraph.pregel.Pregel class with wrapt: invoke, ainvoke, stream and astream. It is not a LangChain callback handler and registers no callbacks. Every runnable graph is a Pregel, so each run produces one span however the graph was built: a compiled StateGraph, create_react_agent, langchain.agents.create_agent, a with_config() copy, a functional-API @entrypoint, a subgraph (nested under its parent's span), or a graph compiled before instrument() was called. Each node execution gets a span too: the instrumentor wraps run_with_retry / arun_with_retry, the functions LangGraph runs every node task through. Those are LangGraph internals; on a version that moves them, node spans are skipped and graph spans are unaffected.

Span types: langgraph.graph.invoke, langgraph.graph.ainvoke, langgraph.graph.stream, langgraph.graph.astream, and langgraph.node.<name> per node execution.

What to expect:

  • session.id, langgraph.session.id and gen_ai.conversation.id are a session_id in the input state, else the enclosing genai_otel.session() block, else the config thread_id, otherwise a random id per run. Node, LLM and tool spans inherit it. langgraph.thread_id and langgraph.recursion_limit are recorded when present in the config.
  • Graph spans carry the graph's shape (langgraph.node_count, langgraph.nodes, langgraph.edge_count, langgraph.channels) and the input and output keys.
  • Node spans carry langgraph.node, langgraph.step and langgraph.triggers, and the node's LLM and tool calls nest beneath them. A node that raises is marked as an error; one that pauses with interrupt() is not, and carries langgraph.node.interrupted. __start__ gets no span.
  • For the Arize AX agent graph, node spans also carry graph.node.id (the node name), metadata ({"langgraph_node", "langgraph_step"}) and openinference.span.kind=CHAIN, and the graph span is the root node, named after the graph (compile(name=...), default LangGraph). See Arize AX.
  • Tools have no span of their own. LLM spans, tokens and cost come from the provider instrumentor enabled alongside (openai above); graph and node spans carry no token usage, so nothing is counted twice.
  • A stream span starts at the first chunk and ends when the stream is exhausted, closed or abandoned. A stream that is never iterated produces no span.
  • Enabling langchain as well adds a langchain.chat_model.* span around each model call. Usage stays on the provider span.

See LangGraph example.

docs.title: Google ADK
docs.text:
Google Agent Development Kit instrumentation.

pip install genai-otel-instrument[google-adk]

Instruments Runner.run_async() and InMemoryRunner.run_debug() with one span per run (google_adk.runner.run / google_adk.runner.run_debug). ADK traces itself through the global tracer provider, so its own spans (ADK 2.x: invoke_workflow, invoke_agent, generate_content, execute_tool) sit under the run span, in one trace per run, including handoffs between agents.

The run span carries:

  • session.id and gen_ai.conversation.id (the ADK session), the app name, tools and sub-agents;
  • gen_ai.agent.name: the agent the run started at. On a later turn of a conversation that was handed off, ADK starts at the agent that answered last, not at the root, which is kept as google_adk.root_agent.name;
  • google_adk.final_agent.name (the agent that answered), google_adk.agents (in order of first appearance), google_adk.transfers (from>to), google_adk.transfer_count, google_adk.invocation_id and google_adk.event_count;
  • with content capture on, google_adk.input_message and google_adk.output (the final answer).

It carries no token counts: ADK's model-call spans and the model instrumentors (Gemini, LiteLLM) already do.

A caller may stop iterating early (for example, break on event.is_final_response()). The run span then ends with genai.stream.closed_early=true, and the next turn starts a trace of its own.

Content. With content capture off (the default), the run span carries no message text, and ADK_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT_IN_SPANS is set to false unless your application set it. That covers ADK's legacy span schema (ADK_TELEMETRY_SCHEMA_VERSION_OPT_IN=1), whose call_llm spans otherwise record the full model request and response. ADK's default schema records message content only under OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT, which this library's content setting also follows.

See Google ADK example.

docs.text:

import genai_otel

docs.title: AutoGen (Legacy)
docs.text:
Multi-agent conversations with group chats, for the import autogen API. Verified against pyautogen 0.2.35 and 0.9, and autogen 0.14.1.

The extra installs pyautogen below 0.10. From 0.10 on, pyautogen is an empty proxy for autogen-agentchat and has no autogen module; use AutoGen AgentChat for that API.

import genai_otel

genai_otel.instrument(
    service_name="autogen-example",
    enabled_instrumentors=["autogen", "openai"],
)

import autogen

llm_config = {"config_list": [{"model": "gpt-4o-mini"}], "max_tokens": 30, "cache_seed": None}

assistant = autogen.AssistantAgent(
    name="assistant",
    llm_config=llm_config,
    system_message="Answer in at most 6 words.",
)

user_proxy = autogen.UserProxyAgent(
    name="user",
    human_input_mode="NEVER",
    max_consecutive_auto_reply=1,
    code_execution_config=False,
)

user_proxy.initiate_chat(
    assistant,
    message="What is the capital of France?",
    max_turns=1,
)
# autogen.initiate_chat -> openai.chat.completion

Instrumented methods:

  • ConversableAgent.initiate_chat() - agent-to-agent conversations (autogen.initiate_chat)
  • GroupChat.select_speaker() - speaker selection (autogen.group_chat.select_speaker)
  • GroupChatManager.run_chat() - group chat orchestration (autogen.group_chat.run)

Tokens and cost are on the LLM spans. a_initiate_chat() is not traced yet.

docs.title: AutoGen AgentChat (v0.4+)
docs.text:
Verified against autogen-agentchat 0.7.5.

pip install genai-otel-instrument[autogen-agentchat] "autogen-ext[openai]"

import asyncio

import genai_otel

genai_otel.instrument(
    service_name="agentchat-example",
    enabled_instrumentors=["autogen_agentchat", "openai"],
)

from autogen_agentchat.agents import AssistantAgent
from autogen_ext.models.openai import OpenAIChatCompletionClient


async def get_weather(city: str) -> str:
    """Return the current weather for a city."""
    return "Sunny, 21 C in {0}".format(city)


async def main():
    client = OpenAIChatCompletionClient(model="gpt-4o-mini", max_tokens=40)
    agent = AssistantAgent(
        name="weather_agent",
        model_client=client,
        tools=[get_weather],
        system_message="Use the get_weather tool, then answer in under 10 words.",
        reflect_on_tool_use=True,
    )
    await agent.run(task="What is the weather in Paris?")
    await client.close()


asyncio.run(main())
# autogen_agentchat.agent.run -> invoke_agent weather_agent (AutoGen's own span)
#   -> autogen_agentchat.agent.on_messages -> openai.chat.completion

Span types:

  • autogen_agentchat.agent.run, autogen_agentchat.agent.run_stream - agent name and type, model, task
  • autogen_agentchat.agent.on_messages - under run, or for a direct call
  • autogen_agentchat.team.run, autogen_agentchat.team.run_stream - team type, participants, termination condition, stop reason

What to expect:

  • Tokens and cost are on the LLM spans; agent and team spans carry none.
  • AutoGen 0.7 emits its own OpenTelemetry spans through the same tracer provider, so they appear in the same trace: create_agent, invoke_agent and execute_tool (scope autogen-core), plus one span per runtime message (scope autogen SingleThreadedAgentRuntime). A two-agent team run produced 32 of the runtime spans; AUTOGEN_DISABLE_RUNTIME_TRACING=true, set before the team is created, removes them.
  • If you stop reading a run_stream() early, call await stream.aclose() so its span ends there.

docs.title: Pydantic AI
docs.text:
Type-safe agents with Pydantic validation and multi-provider support. Verified against Pydantic AI 2.55.0.

pip install genai-otel-instrument[pydantic-ai]

import genai_otel

genai_otel.instrument(
    service_name="my-pydantic-ai-app",
    enabled_instrumentors=["pydantic_ai", "openai"],
)

from pydantic import BaseModel
from pydantic_ai import Agent


class CityInfo(BaseModel):
    city: str
    country: str


agent = Agent(
    "openai:gpt-4o-mini",
    name="city_agent",
    instructions="Call get_country exactly once, then give the final answer.",
    output_type=CityInfo,
)


@agent.tool_plain
def get_country(city: str) -> str:
    """Return the country a city is in."""
    return {"paris": "France", "rome": "Italy"}.get(city.lower(), "Unknown")


result = agent.run_sync("Which country is Paris in?")
print(result.output)
# pydantic_ai.agent.run_sync -> pydantic_ai.agent.run -> openai.responses (one per model request)

Span types:

Call Spans agent.run_sync() pydantic_ai.agent.run_sync -> pydantic_ai.agent.run -> LLM spans await agent.run(), agent.run_stream_events() pydantic_ai.agent.run -> LLM spans agent.run_stream(), agent.run_stream_sync() pydantic_ai.agent.run_stream, open for the whole block agent.iter() pydantic_ai.agent.iter -> LLM spans

What to expect:

  • Agent spans carry the agent name, model, tool names, output type, response model and finish reason.
  • Tokens and cost are on the LLM spans (openai.responses for openai: models, openai.chat.completion for openai-chat:). With only pydantic_ai enabled, the agent span carries the run totals itself.
  • Tool executions have no span of their own.
  • Concurrent runs (asyncio.gather) are separate traces.
  • Pydantic AI's own instrumentation (Agent.instrument_all()) is off by default. If you turn it on as well, its invoke_agent, chat and execute_tool spans appear in the same trace and every model request is reported twice. Enable one or the other.
  • Pydantic AI prints a one-time observability: off banner because it does not detect TraceVerde; PYDANTIC_AI_NO_BANNER=1 hides it.

See Pydantic AI example.

docs.title: Strands Harness
docs.text:
Native instrumentation for the optional Strands Harness runtime. It uses the Harness hook API to preserve agent, delegated-agent, model, tool, MCP, and context-compaction relationships while allowing the Strands SDK's own provider spans to remain in place.

pip install 'genai-otel-instrument[strands]'

import genai_otel

genai_otel.instrument(
    service_name="my-strands-app",
    enabled_instrumentors=["strands"],
    enable_content_capture=False,
)

from strands_harness import create_harness

agent = create_harness(instructions="Answer in one paragraph.", session=True)
result = agent("Explain OpenTelemetry.")

The logical hierarchy is harness.run -> agent.run, with llm.request, tool.call, mcp.call, context.compaction, and subagent.run children when those operations are exposed by the installed Harness version. Prompts, tool arguments/results, MCP payloads, memory contents, and model output are omitted unless the existing GenAI content-capture setting is enabled. Provider-level spans are enriched when active, avoiding duplicate model/tool spans. The extra currently targets strands-harness>=0.1.1 on Python 3.10+.

See the Strands Harness example.

docs.title: Anthropic Claude Agent SDK
docs.text:
The Claude Agent SDK is distinct from Anthropic's Messages API client. This integration uses the maintained OpenInference adapter to trace query() and ClaudeSDKClient turns, tool hooks, and delegated subagents.

pip install 'genai-otel-instrument[claude-agent-sdk]'

import genai_otel

genai_otel.instrument(
    service_name="claude-agent-app",
    enabled_instrumentors=["claude_agent_sdk"],
    enable_content_capture=False,

import asyncio
from claude_agent_sdk import ClaudeAgentOptions, query


async def main():
    async for message in query(
        "List Python files in the current directory.",
        options=ClaudeAgentOptions(allowed_tools=["Glob"]),
    ):
        if hasattr(message, "result"):
            print(message.result)


asyncio.run(main())

Agent and tool spans include SDK-reported token usage when present; the configured cost enricher prices those counts when the model is in the pricing catalog. The Claude Agent SDK runs the model through its own CLI process, so the ordinary Anthropic Messages instrumentor does not see its internal requests. The adapter's agent span carries usage; it does not claim separate LLM request spans. Do not enable a second Claude Agent SDK instrumentor alongside this integration.

docs.title: Voice Agents: Pipecat and LiveKit Agents
docs.text:
For a voice agent the questions that matter are about timing: how long after the user stopped speaking the agent started, who interrupted whom, and how much dead air there was. A transcript keeps the words but loses the timing. Both frameworks trace themselves through the global tracer provider, so their spans reach the same backend as this library's once instrument() has run. The pipecat and livekit_agents instrumentors (on by default, and inactive unless the framework is installed) add one turn shape to both.

Pipecat (1.15+) LiveKit Agents (1.8+) Who spoke when voice.turn spans under a voice.conversation span, from the pipeline's speaking frames LiveKit's own user_speaking / agent_speaking spans get the voice.turn.* attributes Conversation totals on voice.conversation on LiveKit's agent_session Content with capture off Pipecat's input, output, transcript, text, gen_ai.system_instructions, tools and tools.definitions are removed from its spans LIVEKIT_TELEMETRY_ALLOW_PII=false is set unless your application set it, so LiveKit withholds transcripts itself

A speaker turn is the audible interval, from first to last audio. Each turn carries:

  • voice.turn.speaker (user / agent), voice.turn.index, voice.turn.duration_ms and voice.turn.overlap_ms;
  • voice.turn.interrupted: the turn was cut off by the other party. On a user turn the agent interrupted; on an agent turn the user barged in. Overlap that does not end the turn (an "mm-hm") is overlap, not an interruption. voice.turn.interrupted.source is framework or derived;
  • on agent turns, voice.turn.response_latency_ms: the time from the end of the user turn it answers to the agent's first audio, with that turn's index as voice.turn.answers_turn.

The conversation carries voice.turn_count.user / .agent, voice.user_talk_ms, voice.agent_talk_ms, voice.agent_talk_share, voice.silence_ms, voice.dead_air_ms, voice.dead_air_count, voice.dead_air_max_ms, voice.interruption_count (the agent cut the user off), voice.barge_in_count (the user cut the agent off), and the response-latency median and maximum. Dead air is a gap longer than GENAI_VOICE_DEAD_AIR_MS (default 2000).

No audio and no text go on these spans. Pipecat's own exchange-level turn spans and its STT, LLM and TTS spans are kept. The model calls inside them are this library's provider spans, which nest under Pipecat's, so tokens are counted once.

For an application with its own audio loop, the same shape:

import genai_otel

with genai_otel.voice_conversation(conversation_id=call_id) as conv:
    with conv.turn("user"):           # from the first to the last user audio
        ...
    conv.add_turn("agent", start=t2, end=t3)   # or with times known afterwards (epoch seconds)

docs.title: A2A (Agent2Agent)
docs.text:
A2A is the protocol agents use to call each other: discover an agent through its Agent Card, send it a message, follow the task it runs. The a2a instrumentor covers the official Python SDK, a2a-sdk 1.0 or later (pip install a2a-sdk). It is on by default and does nothing when the SDK is absent or older than 1.0.

import genai_otel

genai_otel.instrument()   # before the first `import a2a`, see "The SDK's own spans" below

from a2a.client.client_factory import ClientFactory
# ... build the client and call send_message as usual

What you get

  • A CLIENT span per client call (send_message, get_task, list_tasks, cancel_task, subscribe, get_extended_agent_card and the push-notification config calls), named {a2a.method.name} {agent name}. A streaming call's span ends when the stream does. It also carries gen_ai.operation.name=invoke_agent and the target's gen_ai.agent.name, so an agent graph can draw the edge from the calling agent to the called one.
  • A server side for the SDK's request handlers (DefaultRequestHandler, its v2 and legacy forms, and so the JSON-RPC, REST and gRPC bindings). When an HTTP or gRPC server span is already current (FastAPI, Starlette, ASGI or gRPC instrumentation), the A2A attributes go on that span, and an HTTP one is renamed to {method} {agent}. Only when there is none does a SERVER span open.
  • One trace across both agents. The client injects W3C traceparent / tracestate through the SDK's ClientCallInterceptor hook (headers over HTTP, metadata over gRPC), and the server joins that trace when no transport instrumentation did. Baggage follows the session-baggage rules: nothing but the ids you named in GENAI_SESSION_BAGGAGE_KEYS leaves the process as session.id / user.id. GENAI_A2A_PROPAGATE=false turns propagation off.

Attributes

Attribute Notes a2a.method.name SendMessage, SendStreamingMessage, GetTask, CancelTask, SubscribeToTask ... a2a.protocol.version From the Agent Card interface in use (client spans) a2a.protocol.binding Provisional. jsonrpc, grpc or http_json. OpenTelemetry has not settled how to record the binding (semantic-conventions-genai issue 612); this name may change a2a.tenant, a2a.message.id, a2a.message.reference_task_ids From the request a2a.task.id, a2a.task.state State is one of submitted, working, completed, failed, canceled, input_required, rejected, auth_required gen_ai.conversation.id The A2A contextId gen_ai.agent.name / .description / .version From the Agent Card server.address, server.port From the card's interface URL (client spans) error.type The A2A error name (TaskNotFoundError), else the HTTP or gRPC status a2a.message.{text,file,data}_part_count, a2a.response.{text,file,data}_part_count, a2a.artifact.count, a2a.agent.skill_count genai_otel additions: counts, never content

A task id, context id or state that takes several values during one operation (a stream that goes submitted, working, completed) is left off rather than guessed.

What is recorded, and when

Always Only with content capture on (OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=true or GENAI_ENABLE_CONTENT_CAPTURE=true) Never Ids, task states, counts of parts by kind, the artifact count, file media types, the Agent Card's name, description and version, the skill count Message and artifact text (a2a.message.text, a2a.response.text), data parts (a2a.message.data, a2a.response.data), skill names (a2a.agent.skill_names) File bytes, file URLs and file names

Failed tasks are not errors. A task that ends failed or rejected sets a2a.task.state and leaves the span status alone: the call worked, and the agent's answer was no. A raised error (a JSON-RPC error, a gRPC status, an HTTP error) marks the span ERROR.

The SDK's own spans. a2a-sdk makes spans of its own, named after Python modules and carrying no A2A attributes, with its internal queues marked SERVER. The instrumentor sets OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_A2A_SDK_ENABLED=false to stop them, unless you set that variable yourself. The SDK reads it once, when a2a.utils.telemetry is first imported, so genai_otel.instrument() has to run before your application imports a2a. If a2a is already imported the SDK's spans stay on beside ours, and one INFO line says so; set the variable in the environment to fix that.

Limits. Python SDK 1.x only. Client wrapping covers the SDK's BaseClient (what ClientFactory returns); a custom Client subclass is not wrapped. Server wrapping covers DefaultRequestHandler (V2) and LegacyRequestHandler; a handler you write yourself on RequestHandler is not. No A2A metrics yet: the OpenTelemetry convention for them is still open. The Java, Go, JavaScript and .NET SDKs are not covered.

docs.title: A2UI (Agent-to-UI)
docs.text:
A2UI is Google's open protocol for an agent to send a user interface as declarative JSON instead of code. The agent describes surfaces and components from a catalog the client trusts, the client draws them with its own native components, and sends the user's actions back. It usually travels inside A2A messages. The protocol defines no telemetry, so the a2ui.* attributes below are genai_otel additions and provisional.

What it makes visible: UI the renderer rejected (a validation error the server never sees), UI the agent SDK could not parse (the model wrote invalid output and the user sees nothing), what the user did (an action starts the agent's next turn), and what was shown.

It is on by default. GENAI_A2UI_ENABLED=false turns it off without touching A2A.

Inside A2A spans (a2a-sdk 1.x). When an A2A message, stream event or artifact carries an A2UI data part (mimeType application/a2ui+json, or the deprecated application/json+a2ui, in the part's metadata or its media type), the A2A span gains a2ui.* attributes. The payload may be one message or a list of messages per part; both shapes are read. What the renderer sent (the request) counts as a2ui.renderer_message.count, what the agent sent (the response, stream events and artifacts) as a2ui.agent_message.count. a2ui.extension.active is set when the A2UI extension URI is among the call's extensions, and the renderer's catalogs are read from a2uiRendererCapabilities or a2uiClientCapabilities in the message metadata. A2UI parts still count in the A2A data part counts. A renderer error message does not make the A2A span ERROR: the call that carried it worked. It sets a2ui.error.codes and adds one a2ui.error span event per error.

The agent SDK (a2ui-agent-sdk 0.11+, any transport). The official A2UI-over-A2A bridge (a2ui-a2a) pins a2a-sdk 0.3, which the A2A instrumentor does not cover, and the SDK also runs under Google ADK and MCP, so the agent SDK is wrapped directly:

Span Wraps Notes a2ui.parse_response A2uiRequestProcessor.parse_response ERROR with error.type and a2ui.validation.outcome=invalid when parsing or validation raises, which is the model producing invalid UI. A child of the LLM span when one is active a2ui.parse_stream A2uiRequestProcessor.open_stream Ends when the stream does (close(), or an error), with the totals. ERROR when a block is rejected, including a stream that reads past it a2ui.process {type} RendererToAgentMessageProcessor.process_message The renderer message (a2ui.process action), the reply count (a2ui.agent_message.count) and the error codes of renderer errors and function errors (current span) a2ui.a2a.parts.parse_content_to_parts That function swallows every exception and logs only its class. The current span gets a2ui.validation.outcome=invalid and an a2ui.validation_failed event with error.type. Return value and logging are unchanged. Needs a2ui-a2a

It does nothing when a2ui-agent-sdk is not installed or is older than 0.11. v1.0 and v0.9 messages are read; v0.8 messages are recognised and counted, and their shapes are not parsed.

What is recorded, and when

Always Only with content capture on Never Message types, protocol version, surface and catalog ids, counts, component count, action and function names, error codes, the validation outcome a2ui.messages (the JSON), data-model values, an action's context, an error's path and message (a validation message can quote user data), component type names The content of image or file URLs inside components, and data: URIs

Action names are developer-defined identifiers, like span names. Component type names in a custom catalog can describe a business process, so they are content. A single-valued key (a2ui.surface.id, a2ui.catalog.id, a2ui.action.name, a2ui.function.name, a2ui.protocol.version) is left off when one operation saw several distinct values; the list keys are sorted and de-duplicated.

Limits. Python only: there is no Python renderer, and the prompt-building parts of the agent SDK are not instrumented (the LLM span already records the prompt under content capture). a2ui-a2a's A2A 0.3 spans are not produced (the A2A instrumentor covers a2a-sdk 1.x); the agent SDK spans cover the A2UI signal there. A function imported before instrumentation (from a2ui.a2a.parts import parse_content_to_parts) keeps the unwrapped reference, so call it through the module or instrument first. A stream that is never closed ends its span when it is garbage collected.

docs.title: Multimodal Observability
docs.text: genai-otel-instrument v1.0.0 adds first-class capture of multimodal content — images, audio, video, and documents — alongside the existing text instrumentation. Multimodal payloads never appear inline in span attributes; bytes are offloaded to a configured store and referenced by URI.

docs.title: Why this exists
docs.text: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions standardize text prompts/completions but do not standardize how multimodal attachments — images, audio, video, documents — are captured on spans. This library defines that shape with an additive, OTel-compatible attribute namespace plus a pluggable offload pipeline so binary content lives in your object store, not in span attributes. (The upstream proposal is filed with open-telemetry/semantic-conventions as issue #3672.)

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
pip install 'genai-otel-instrument[multimodal,openai,anthropic,google]'

export GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_CAPTURE_MODE=full
export GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_STORE=minio
export GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_STORE_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:9000
export GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_STORE_BUCKET=genai-otel-media
export GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_STORE_ACCESS_KEY=...
export GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_STORE_SECRET_KEY=...

For an on-premises SeaweedFS S3 gateway, select the seaweed store name. The SDK uses path-style S3 addressing for this backend; set the endpoint to the gateway, commonly port 8333, and ensure the bucket exists and the credentials can write objects to it.

export GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_STORE=seaweed
export GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_STORE_ENDPOINT=https://seaweed-s3.example.internal:8333
export GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_STORE_BUCKET=genai-otel-media
export GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_STORE_ACCESS_KEY=...
export GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_STORE_SECRET_KEY=...

The SDK's own media uploads are not traced as s3.* spans by default, so they do not clutter your traces; the calls run with OpenTelemetry's standard instrumentation suppression active. Set GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_STORE_TRACE_CALLS=true to get nested S3 client spans for the uploads again. Your own S3 calls are always traced. See SeaweedFS for labelling the gateway.

from genai_otel import instrument
instrument()

# Any subsequent OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / Groq call with multimodal content
# automatically emits content-part attributes and uploads bytes to MinIO.

docs.title: Capture modes
docs.text:
GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_CAPTURE_MODE Behaviour off (default) No multimodal attributes emitted. Identical to pre-1.0.0. reference_only Modality + MIME + byte size captured. Bytes NOT stored. full Redact (if configured) → upload to store → reference by URI.

off is the default to preserve byte-identical behaviour for existing users. BFSI deployments that want to record multimodal presence without storing bytes should use reference_only. Production deployments that want full traceability + UI rendering use full plus a store.

docs.title: Store backends
docs.text:
Set via GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_STORE:

Value Notes none (default) No offload. Works with capture_mode=reference_only. filesystem Local directory. MEDIA_STORE_ENDPOINT is the root path. s3 / minio / seaweed S3-compatible object storage. Requires the multimodal-s3 extra. seaweed selects path-style addressing for a SeaweedFS S3 gateway. http PUTs to a configured base URL (self-hosted ingest gateways).

Per-blob size is capped by GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_MAX_BYTES (default 10 MiB). Oversized blobs are recorded with gen_ai.media.stripped_reason="size_exceeded" and the bytes are dropped.

docs.title: Redactors
docs.text:
Redactors run on raw bytes before upload, per modality. Built-ins:

  • genai_otel.media.redactors.exif_stripper — removes EXIF/metadata from images. Requires Pillow.
  • genai_otel.media.redactors.face_blur — Haar-cascade face detection + Gaussian blur. Requires opencv-python-headless.
  • genai_otel.media.redactors.pdf_pii_redact — regex-based PII removal in PDFs. Requires pypdf.

Plug one in:

export GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_REDACTOR=genai_otel.media.redactors.face_blur

Or write your own:

def my_redactor(modality: str, mime_type: str, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    if modality == "image":
        return strip_pii_from_image(data)
    return data

export GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_REDACTOR=mypkg.my_redactor

If the redactor raises, the bytes are dropped and stripped_reason=redactor_error is recorded — fail-closed, never fail-open with unredacted bytes.

docs.title: Span attribute reference
docs.text:
For every multimodal message, the instrumentor emits:

Attribute Example gen_ai.prompt.{n}.role user gen_ai.prompt.{n}.content.{m}.type text | image | audio | video | document gen_ai.prompt.{n}.content.{m}.text text parts only gen_ai.prompt.{n}.content.{m}.media_uri s3://bucket/key or https://... gen_ai.prompt.{n}.content.{m}.media_mime_type image/png gen_ai.prompt.{n}.content.{m}.media_byte_size 123456 gen_ai.prompt.{n}.content.{m}.media_source inline_offloaded | external_url | reference_only gen_ai.media.stripped_reason size_exceeded, modality_not_allowed, redactor_error, upload_error

The gen_ai.completion.* namespace mirrors this for generated content (e.g. image generation output, TTS responses).
