docs.title: Real-world application examples
docs.text:
Release validation should use application-shaped inputs, not only spans assembled from isolated attribute fixtures. The repository includes a vendor-key-free replay of a banking voice-RAG turn:

examples/real_world/voice_rag_replay.py

The replay reads an actual WAV recording and a knowledge-base corpus. It emits one trace containing separate speech-to-text, local embedding, retrieval, and grounded-answer spans. Audio is attached only to the speech span and must be represented as type=audio with media_mime_type=audio/wav.

Run it against the remote collector:

python examples/real_world/voice_rag_replay.py `
  --audio <path-to>/account_balance.wav `
  --corpus <path-to>/kb_corpus.py `
  --transcript "Please check my account balance and recent transactions." `
  --endpoint http://<collector-host>:4318

The example does not claim to call an ASR, embedding, vector database, or LLM vendor. It validates the telemetry path with the application payload shape while remaining runnable without paid credentials. Use deterministic lab fixtures for the WAV and corpus, not production customer data.

docs.title: Document OCR
docs.text:
The companion replay covers the other multimodal workflow: PDF/image ingestion and structured document extraction.

python examples/real_world/document_ocr_replay.py `
  --document <path-to>/invoice.pdf `
  --endpoint http://<collector-host>:4318

The emitted OCR span must report type=document and media_mime_type=application/pdf for a PDF. An image input must report type=image and its image MIME type. Use --no-export for a local shape-only check. This replay validates file handling and telemetry; it does not claim that a provider-backed OCR model ran.

A full voice-RAG application runs ASR → embedding → vector retrieval → reranking → grounded answer → TTS, and an OCR application runs document bytes through multimodal extraction. These replays cover the telemetry shape of both without the providers.

docs.title: Retrieval quality
docs.text: TraceVerde emits the existing retrieval.* and db.vector.* attributes for the retrieved documents and requested top-k. The additive rag.* attributes describe quality and provenance signals that an application or vector instrumentor can know at retrieval time.

docs.title: Quality attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Meaning rag.embedding.model Model used for the query embedding rag.embedding.index_model Model used to build the index rag.embedding.model_match Boolean comparison of the two model identifiers rag.embedding.dim Query/index vector dimension rag.search.score_floor Minimum score accepted by the search rag.search.distance Distance or similarity metric name rag.result.score_max / min / mean Distribution summary for returned scores rag.result.score_margin Difference between the two highest scores rag.corpus.version Corpus or index version rag.context.tokens_est Estimated context tokens sent downstream rag.context.truncated Whether context was truncated rag.answer.refused Whether the answer path refused to answer

top_k and result count remain db.vector.top_k and retrieval.document_count; TraceVerde does not emit duplicate rag.* names for those values.

docs.title: Application-owned signals
docs.text:
Use the public helper when the application owns the embedding, index metadata, or answer policy:

instrumentor.add_retrieval_quality_attributes(
    span,
    embedding_model="text-embedding-3-small",
    index_embedding_model="text-embedding-3-small",
    embedding_dim=1536,
    distance="cosine",
    scores=[0.91, 0.84, 0.72],
    corpus_version="2026-08-20",
    context_tokens_est=1200,
    context_truncated=False,
    answer_refused=False,
)

gen_ai.rag.context is not emitted by the library. It is an application-set input consumed by the evaluation processors, so applications that use hallucination evaluation should continue to set it explicitly.

docs.title: Sarvam AI
docs.text: TraceVerde provides full instrumentation for Sarvam AI, India's sovereign AI platform for multi-modal Indian language processing.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install genai-otel-instrument[sarvamai]
pip install sarvamai

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
import genai_otel
genai_otel.instrument(service_name="sarvam-app")

from sarvamai import SarvamAI

client = SarvamAI(api_subscription_key="your_key")

# Chat completion with sarvam-m
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="sarvam-m",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What is AI?"}],
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
# Traces, tokens, and costs captured automatically

docs.title: Chat (sarvam-m)
docs.text:
Sarvam's multilingual chat model with support for Indian languages.

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="sarvam-m",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant who speaks Hindi."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Tell me about India's space program"},
    ],
)

docs.title: Translation (Mayura v1)
docs.text:
Translation across 22+ Indian languages with speaker gender adaptation.

translation = client.text.translate(
    input="Hello, how are you?",
    source_language_code="en-IN",
    target_language_code="hi-IN",
    model="mayura:v1",
    mode="classic-formal",
    speaker_gender="female",
)
print(translation.translated_text)

Features:

  • 22+ Indian languages
  • mayura:v1 (latest) and sarvam-translate:v1 (legacy)
  • Translation modes: classic-formal, classic-colloquial
  • Speaker gender adaptation
  • Numerals format control (international vs native)

See Mayura translation example.

docs.title: Text-to-Speech (Bulbul v3)
docs.text:
High-quality TTS with 48 speakers across 11 Indian languages.

tts_response = client.text.speech(
    input="Namaste, aap kaise hain?",
    target_language_code="hi-IN",
    model="bulbul:v2",
    speaker="meera",
    pace=1.0,
    pitch=0,
    loudness=1.5,
)
# tts_response.audios contains base64-encoded WAV audio

Bulbul v3 features:

  • 48 speakers (male and female voices)
  • 11 Indian languages
  • Pace control (0.5 to 2.0)
  • Temperature control for expressiveness
  • 24000 Hz sample rate
  • Max 2500 characters per request

See Bulbul v3 TTS example.

docs.title: Speech-to-Text (Saarika)
docs.text:
Automatic speech recognition for Indian languages.

with open("audio.wav", "rb") as f:
    transcript = client.speech.text(
        file=f,
        model="saarika:v2",
        language_code="hi-IN",
    )
print(transcript.transcript)

docs.title: Language Detection
docs.text:
Identify the language of input text.

detection = client.text.detect_language(
    input="Namaste, kaise ho?",
)
print(detection.language_code)  # "hi-IN"

docs.title: Multilingual Pipeline Example
docs.text:
A full production-style pipeline combining multiple Sarvam APIs:

Customer Query (any Indian language)
  +-- Language Detection
  +-- Translate to English
  +-- sarvam-m Chat (generate response)
  +-- Translate response back to customer's language
  +-- Bulbul v3 TTS (voice response)

All steps are automatically traced with cost breakdown per API call.

docs.title: SeaweedFS
docs.text: The SDK traces SeaweedFS through its S3 gateway (boto3, aiobotocore, aioboto3, s3fs) and through the Filer HTTP API (httpx, aiohttp). SeaweedFS is recognised only on endpoints you declare; nothing is guessed from a port number or a response header.

docs.title: Declare your endpoints
docs.text:
# Comma-separated host[:port] or URLs. A bare host matches any port; "*.suffix" hosts allowed.
export GENAI_OTEL_SEAWEEDFS_ENDPOINTS=seaweed-s3.example.internal:8333,seaweed-filer.example.internal:8888

When GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_STORE=seaweed, the media-store endpoint is declared automatically.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
S3 gateway spans (s3.<Operation>) keep db.system="s3" and gain:

  • db.system.name="seaweedfs" when the endpoint is declared;
  • server.port (always, for any S3 endpoint);
  • aws.s3.bucket, aws.s3.key (the legacy s3.bucket / s3.object are still emitted but deprecated) and aws.request_id.

Filer spans (seaweedfs.filer.<operation>, client kind) for requests to declared hosts:

Attribute Value db.system.name seaweedfs db.operation.name upload, append, download, list, stat, delete, delete_recursive, move, copy, mkdir, tag, other http.request.method, http.response.status_code as sent / received server.address, server.port declared host and port url.path.prefix first 2 path segments only (GENAI_OTEL_SEAWEEDFS_PATH_PREFIX_SEGMENTS) seaweedfs.request.size, seaweedfs.response.size from Content-Length when stated

File contents, file names beyond the prefix, query values, headers and error text are never recorded. A 404 on stat or download is not marked as an error.

requests is not patched (patching it can break OTLP HTTP exporters), so Filer calls made with requests are not traced. Use httpx or aiohttp, or the S3 gateway.

docs.title: Async S3 clients
docs.text: aiobotocore, aioboto3 and s3fs calls are traced as s3.<Operation> spans exactly like boto3 calls, when aiobotocore is installed.

docs.title: The SDK's own media uploads
docs.text: Uploads made by the multimodal media store are not traced by default. Set GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_STORE_TRACE_CALLS=true to see them as nested s3.* spans.

docs.title: Filter examples
docs.text:
db.system.name = "seaweedfs"
name = "seaweedfs.filer.upload" and http.response.status_code >= 500

docs.title: Speech telemetry
docs.text:
Speech spans use the same operation vocabulary across local and hosted instrumentors:

  • ASR: gen_ai.operation.name and gen_ai.request.type are speech_to_text.
  • TTS: gen_ai.operation.name and gen_ai.request.type are text_to_speech.
  • gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.request.language_code, gen_ai.request.voice_id, gen_ai.request.audio.sample_rate, gen_ai.request.streamed, and gen_ai.response.output_format are shared where the provider exposes them.
  • gen_ai.usage.audio_duration_seconds records measured or provider-reported audio duration. ASR spans may also include gen_ai.response.transcript_length, gen_ai.response.language_code, and gen_ai.audio.real_time_factor.
  • Streaming TTS and audio-generation spans record gen_ai.server.time_to_first_token when the first audio chunk is observed. Non-streaming calls leave this attribute unset; zero is not a valid proxy for an unmeasured first-byte time.

The Hugging Face instrumentor covers the automatic-speech-recognition pipeline and direct audio model generation. The optional liquid_audio instrumentor covers Liquid AI's LFM2AudioModel generator methods. Install it with:

pip install "genai-otel-instrument[liquid-audio]"

Sarvam-specific sarvam.tts.* and sarvam.stt.* attributes remain available alongside the portable attributes.

docs.title: Performance Tuning Guide
docs.text: This guide covers configuration options for optimizing genai-otel-instrument in production.

docs.title: Import Time
docs.text: The library uses lazy imports. import genai_otel loads in ~20ms. Heavy modules (OTel SDK, instrumentors, GPU metrics) are only loaded when you call genai_otel.instrument() or access specific classes.

docs.title: Sampling Rate
docs.text:
Reduce telemetry volume by sampling a fraction of traces:

# Only trace 10% of requests
export GENAI_SAMPLING_RATE=0.1

from genai_otel import instrument
instrument(sampling_rate=0.1)  # 10% of traces

A sampling rate of 1.0 (default) traces everything. Set to 0.0 to disable tracing entirely.

docs.title: Batch Export Configuration
docs.text:
The library uses BatchSpanProcessor and PeriodicExportingMetricReader for non-blocking export. OpenTelemetry environment variables control batching:

# Spans: max batch size and export interval
export OTEL_BSP_MAX_EXPORT_BATCH_SIZE=512    # default: 512
export OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY_MILLIS=5000   # default: 5000ms
export OTEL_BSP_MAX_QUEUE_SIZE=2048          # default: 2048

# Metrics: export interval
export OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL=60000     # default: 60000ms (1 min)

For high-throughput applications, increase MAX_QUEUE_SIZE and MAX_EXPORT_BATCH_SIZE.

docs.title: Content Capture
docs.text:
Capturing prompt/response content adds overhead to span size and export bandwidth:

# Disable content capture for lower overhead
export GENAI_ENABLE_CONTENT_CAPTURE=false

# Or limit content length (default: 1000 chars)
export GENAI_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH=200

docs.title: GPU Metrics
docs.text:
GPU metrics collection runs in a background thread. Disable if not needed:

export GENAI_ENABLE_GPU_METRICS=false

Or adjust collection interval:

export GENAI_GPU_METRICS_INTERVAL=30  # seconds (default: 15)

docs.title: Cost Tracking
docs.text:
Cost calculation adds minimal overhead but can be disabled:

export GENAI_ENABLE_COST_TRACKING=false

docs.title: MCP Instrumentation
docs.text:
Disable database/cache/API instrumentation if not needed:

export GENAI_ENABLE_MCP_INSTRUMENTATION=false

docs.title: Selective Instrumentors
docs.text:
Only enable the instrumentors you need:

# Only instrument OpenAI and Anthropic
export GENAI_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTORS=openai,anthropic

docs.title: OTLP Protocol
docs.text:
HTTP (default) works for most setups. gRPC may offer better performance for high-throughput:

export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4317

docs.title: OTLP Timeout
docs.text:
Increase timeout for slow networks or reduce for faster failure:

export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT=5  # seconds (default: 10)

docs.title: Production Checklist
docs.text:
1. Set GENAI_SAMPLING_RATE to 0.1-0.5 for high-traffic services
  2. Disable GENAI_ENABLE_CONTENT_CAPTURE unless needed for debugging
  3. Set GENAI_ENABLE_GPU_METRICS=false if no GPUs are used
  4. Use GENAI_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTORS to limit to providers you actually use
  5. Set GENAI_FAIL_ON_ERROR=false (default) so instrumentation issues don't crash your app
  6. Configure OTEL_BSP_MAX_QUEUE_SIZE based on your request volume

docs.title: Semantic Conventions
docs.text: TraceVerde follows OpenTelemetry semantic conventions for GenAI with additional custom attributes.

docs.title: GenAI Core (OTel Standard)
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description gen_ai.system string Provider name (e.g., "openai", "anthropic") gen_ai.request.model string Requested model identifier gen_ai.response.model string Actual model used in response gen_ai.request.type string Call type ("chat", "embedding", "completion") gen_ai.usage.input_tokens int Input token count gen_ai.usage.output_tokens int Output token count gen_ai.usage.total_tokens int Total token count gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens int Prompt-cache hits (Anthropic cache_read_input_tokens, OpenAI prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens). Included in gen_ai.usage.input_tokens. gen_ai.usage.cache_write.input_tokens int Prompt-cache writes (Anthropic cache_creation_input_tokens). Current spelling: semantic-conventions-genai#440 renamed cache_creation to cache_write. gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.input_tokens int Superseded spelling of the row above. Emitted alongside it only under OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai/dup (the default). gen_ai.usage.reasoning.output_tokens int Reasoning tokens (OpenAI o1/o3-style completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens). Included in gen_ai.usage.output_tokens. server.address string Host of the model endpoint, derived from the SDK client's base URL. Omitted when the SDK exposes no base URL -- absent means "endpoint unknown", never a guessed vendor host. server.port int Port of the model endpoint. Explicit port when the base URL carries one, otherwise the scheme default. gen_ai.usage.{text,image,audio}.input_tokens int Per-modality input tokens (semantic-conventions-genai#440). A subset of gen_ai.usage.input_tokens -- do not sum alongside it. Absent when the provider reports no breakdown. gen_ai.usage.{text,image,audio}.output_tokens int Per-modality output tokens; subset of gen_ai.usage.output_tokens. gen_ai.usage.{text,image,audio}.cache_read.input_tokens int Per-modality prompt-cache hits. gen_ai.response.finish_reasons string[] Finish reasons as an array (registry spelling). gen_ai.response.finish_reason string Superseded singular form, emitted alongside the array under gen_ai/dup. gen_ai.embeddings.dimension.count int Requested embedding dimensions (registry spelling; supersedes gen_ai.request.dimensions). gen_ai.request.encoding_formats string[] Requested encoding formats as an array (registry spelling; supersedes the singular gen_ai.request.encoding_format). gen_ai.request.seed int Sampling seed, when the caller passed one. gen_ai.request.stream bool Whether the caller requested streaming. gen_ai.request.top_k int Top-k sampling parameter, when passed. gen_ai.request.choice.count int Number of completions requested (n, or Google's candidate_count). gen_ai.output.type string json or text, derived from the caller's response_format.

| gen_ai.agent.token_budget | int | Cumulative token cap configured for the invocation (semantic-conventions-genai#425). | | gen_ai.agent.token_budget.consumed | int | Tokens actually consumed across the invocation's inference calls. | | gen_ai.agent.iteration_budget | int | Configured iteration / turn / recursion limit. | | gen_ai.agent.iteration_budget.consumed | int | Inference calls completed during the invocation. | | gen_ai.latency.time_in_queue | float | Scheduler queue wait, seconds (self-hosted engines). | | gen_ai.latency.time_to_first_token | float | TTFT, seconds. | | gen_ai.latency.e2e | float | End-to-end request latency, seconds. | | gen_ai.latency.time_in_model_prefill | float | Prefill phase duration, seconds. | | gen_ai.latency.time_in_model_decode | float | Decode phase duration, seconds. | | gen_ai.latency.time_in_model_inference | float | Total on-engine inference duration, seconds. | | gen_ai.request.id | string | Engine-assigned request id (vLLM / SGLang). |

Engine latency keys are the de-facto vocabulary, not ours

gen_ai.latency.* is emitted verbatim as vLLM and SGLang define it, and as semantic-conventions-genai#408 proposes standardising. Running vLLM's own OTLP tracing alongside this library therefore yields one vocabulary rather than two to join. These keys are not yet in the registry.

Agent budget consumption and threads

Consumption is accumulated in a context-local frame, so it survives head sampling that drops the child inference spans. A call made on a thread that does not carry the context (a bare threading.Thread) is not counted -- consistent with tracing itself, which would also lose the parent/child span relationship for such a call.

Request parameters are recorded only when the caller passes them

An absent gen_ai.request.* attribute means the application did not set that parameter. The library does not materialise provider defaults, which would report a top_k or seed the application never chose.

| gen_ai.usage.token_count_estimated | bool | true when prompt/completion token counts came from a fallback estimate (e.g. multimodal Ollama responses lacking prompt_eval_count, or HuggingFace vision/audio pipelines that don't surface usage). Absent on spans whose tokens come from the provider response. | | gen_ai.usage.image_count | int | Number of input images counted by the instrumentor for multimodal calls (vision pipelines). | | gen_ai.usage.audio_seconds | float | Total input audio duration in seconds for ASR / audio pipelines. | | gen_ai.usage.audio_duration_seconds | float | Canonical total input audio duration in seconds for speech-to-text and audio pipelines. | | gen_ai.operation.name | string | Operation being performed (chat, embeddings) |

Cost lives under gen_ai.usage.cost.*

Earlier revisions of this page listed gen_ai.cost.amount as the cost attribute. Cost is reported under gen_ai.usage.cost.total and its breakdown. Only the Hyperbolic instrumentor also emits gen_ai.cost.amount, for backwards compatibility with dashboards built against it; do not query it as a general cost attribute, because no other provider sets it.

docs.title: Embeddings
docs.text:
Emitted on embedding spans (openai.embeddings), which are the retrieval half of a RAG trace.

Attribute Type Description gen_ai.request.type string embedding - the value cost lookup dispatches on gen_ai.request.input_count int Number of texts in the request; a batch of chunks counts each one, pre-tokenised input counts as one gen_ai.request.dimensions int Requested vector dimension, when the caller asked for one gen_ai.request.encoding_format string Requested encoding format, when set gen_ai.response.embedding_count int Number of vectors returned gen_ai.response.vector_size int Dimension of the returned vectors embedding.model_name string Embedding model; set only when content capture is enabled embedding.text string The embedded text, truncated to GENAI_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH; set only when content capture is enabled embedding.vector string JSON-encoded vector; off unless capture_embedding_vectors is set, since vectors dominate span size

Token usage and cost are recorded exactly as for chat, priced against the embeddings table rather than the chat one.

docs.title: Retrieval quality
docs.text:
The rag.* attributes are additive to retrieval.* and db.vector.*. They describe embedding provenance, score quality, corpus version, and downstream context policy. top_k and result count remain db.vector.top_k and retrieval.document_count; see the retrieval quality guide.

gen_ai.rag.context is application-owned input for evaluation processors. The library reads it when present but does not emit it automatically.

docs.title: Degradation events
docs.text: Capability downgrades are recorded as a gen_ai.degraded span event rather than an error. The event attributes are gen_ai.degraded.component, gen_ai.degraded.from, gen_ai.degraded.to, gen_ai.degraded.reason, and gen_ai.degraded.recoverable. The span status remains OK when the request successfully completes through the degraded path.

docs.title: Cost Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description gen_ai.usage.cost.total float Total cost in USD gen_ai.usage.cost.prompt float Prompt token cost gen_ai.usage.cost.completion float Completion token cost gen_ai.usage.cost.decision float Decision-model cost, on decision spans only. Equal to cost.total there, so a reader can keep decision spend apart without reading the span kind gen_ai.usage.cost.pricing_source string Where the price came from: table, estimated or unpriced (decision spans: table or unpriced, never estimated) gen_ai.request.model.deprecated bool Set only when the provider has announced the model's retirement gen_ai.request.model.deprecation_note string Retirement date and migration target

Read pricing_source before summing cost

A gen_ai.usage.cost.total of 0.0 is ambiguous on its own — it means either "this call really was free" or "no price could be found for this model". Always read pricing_source alongside it:

Value Meaning table Matched an entry in the shipped pricing file. Billable. estimated No entry; price inferred from the parameter count in the model name via the local-model size tier. Indicative only — do not treat as a billable figure. unpriced No price could be determined. cost.total will be 0.0 and must not be counted as free spend.

A dashboard that sums cost.total without filtering on pricing_source will silently under-report spend for every unpriced model.

docs.title: Decision Spans
docs.text:
Decision-model calls are OpenInference DECISION spans (openinference.span.kind = DECISION). The full attribute table, and which attributes need content capture, is in Decision models.

Attribute Type Recorded decision.system string always: openai, typesafe or custom decision.provider string recognised host, or GENAI_DECISION_PROVIDER decision.model_name, decision.request.model_name, decision.response.model_name string always / when they differ decision.token_count.input, decision.token_count.output int when reported genai.decision.protocol string always: openai_decisions, systemone, granite_adapter, manual genai.decision.question_count, genai.decision.refusal_count int always genai.decision.question.types string[] always genai.decision.input.modalities string[] always: text, image, audio genai.decision.input.audio_seconds double WAV audio inputs genai.decision.option_count int one-question calls genai.decision.question.names string[] content capture on genai.decision.min_confidence double content capture on genai.decision.choice string content capture on, one-question calls genai.decision.confidence, .probability, .score, .margin double content capture on, one-question calls evaluation.skipped_reason string decision_span when the response detectors had no text to read

docs.title: Streaming Latency
docs.text:
Emitted only on streamed calls. On a non-streamed call these attributes are absent, not zero.

Attribute Type Description gen_ai.server.time_to_first_token float Seconds from request start to the first streamed chunk (TTFT) gen_ai.server.time_per_output_token float Seconds per output token after the first (TPOT), (duration - ttft) / max(output_tokens - 1, 1) gen_ai.server.ttft float Superseded spelling of TTFT, still emitted for consumers already reading it gen_ai.streaming.token_count int Number of chunks yielded by the stream (chunks, not tokens) gen_ai.streaming.tpot_unavailable_reason string Why TPOT was omitted; currently only output_token_count_unavailable

An absent TTFT is not a zero

Span duration cannot substitute for TTFT: a fast-starting long answer and a slow-starting short one can share a duration. But a fabricated 0 is worse than nothing — it is indistinguishable from an instant first token and drags down every average it enters.

So these attributes are omitted whenever they were not genuinely measured:

  • Non-streamed calls carry neither attribute.
  • TPOT needs a real output-token count. Some providers only send usage in the final chunk when asked. With OpenAI, for example, pass stream_options={"include_usage": True}; without it the span gets TTFT plus gen_ai.streaming.tpot_unavailable_reason, and no TPOT. The chunk count is not used as a stand-in — chunks are not tokens.
  • Text-to-speech streams report TTFT (time to first audio byte) and never TPOT, having no output tokens to divide by.

Report a missing attribute as "not measured" rather than substituting zero.

docs.title: Agent Graph
docs.text:
Added to every span that carries gen_ai.agent.name, so OpenInference backends (Arize AX, Phoenix) can draw the agent graph. Keys a span already carries are kept. Disable with GENAI_ENABLE_AGENT_GRAPH_ATTRIBUTES=false.

Attribute Type Description agent.name string Agent name, copied from gen_ai.agent.name graph.node.id string Graph node; the agent name, so repeat runs share one node graph.node.name string Node label (OpenInference spelling) graph.node.display_name string Node label (Arize AX spelling) graph.node.parent_id string Node of the nearest enclosing agent; unset on a root agent openinference.span.kind string AGENT

LangGraph node spans (langgraph.node.<name>) carry:

Attribute Type Description langgraph.node string Node name langgraph.step int Superstep the node ran in langgraph.triggers string[] Channels that triggered the node langgraph.node.interrupted bool Set when the node paused with interrupt() graph.node.id string Node name (agent graph attributes enabled) metadata string JSON {"langgraph_node", "langgraph_step"}, the OpenInference key Arize reads for LangGraph openinference.span.kind string CHAIN (also on the graph run span, whose graph.node.id is the graph name)

docs.title: Session Tracking
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description session.id string Session identifier; groups a conversation's traces into one session gen_ai.conversation.id string Same value as session.id (OTel GenAI spelling) user.id string User identifier

Every span gets these from the enclosing genai_otel.session() block, or else from its parent span, so a session resolved on a framework span reaches every span beneath it. A span that already carries a key keeps it. Disable with GENAI_ENABLE_SESSION_PROPAGATION=false.

Between services the ids can travel as W3C baggage under the same keys, when the caller sets GENAI_SESSION_BAGGAGE_KEYS and the callee GENAI_SESSION_BAGGAGE_ACCEPT.

docs.title: Resource Attributes
docs.text:
Every resource attribute is a name from the OpenTelemetry registry. They identify where a span came from, which is what makes it possible to separate traffic per host and per instance when several copies of an application run at once.

Attribute Description service.name Service name service.instance.id Instance identifier. Taken from OTEL_SERVICE_INSTANCE_ID when set, otherwise generated - see Host and Instance Identity deployment.environment.name Environment name telemetry.distro.name "genai-otel-instrument" telemetry.distro.version Package version host.name Hostname of the machine host.arch CPU architecture host.ip Non-loopback IP addresses of the host (array) os.type / os.version Operating system process.pid / process.parent_pid Process identifiers process.command Program that was started process.command_line Full startup command line process.command_args Startup arguments (array) process.executable.name / process.executable.path Interpreter location process.owner User the process runs as (requires psutil) process.runtime.name / .version / .description Python runtime

The host.*, os.* and process.* groups come from the OpenTelemetry SDK's own detectors. This library enables host and os by default via OTEL_EXPERIMENTAL_RESOURCE_DETECTORS; process is opt-in (add it to that variable). host.ip has no upstream detector and is resolved by the library only when GENAI_OTEL_RESOURCE_HOST_IP=true.

Credential values in process.command_args are redacted

A value following a flag whose name looks like a credential (--password, --api-key, --token, --client-secret, ...) is replaced with ***REDACTED***, in both the --flag value and --flag=value forms, as are name=value pairs and scheme://user:password@host URLs. This has to happen in the SDK: process.command_args is an array, so a flag and its value become separate elements and no downstream name=value rule can reconnect them. Redaction is pattern-based and cannot catch a credential passed under an unrecognised flag name - see Host and Instance Identity for how to drop the process detector entirely.

Superseded spellings, still emitted alongside the current names for the same reason the GenAI token attributes are dual-emitted, and removed at 2.0:

Superseded Current environment deployment.environment.name telemetry.auto.name telemetry.distro.name telemetry.auto.version telemetry.distro.version

docs.title: GenAI Metrics
docs.text: Metric Type Unit Description gen_ai.requests Counter requests Request count by provider/model gen_ai.client.token.usage Counter tokens Token usage, labelled token_type (prompt/completion). No longer defined by the conventions; see Token usage metrics gen_ai.client.operation.duration Histogram seconds Request latency gen_ai.cost Counter USD Estimated costs gen_ai.errors Counter errors Error count by type gen_ai.server.time_to_first_token Histogram seconds TTFT, recorded on streamed calls only gen_ai.server.time_per_output_token Histogram seconds TPOT, recorded when the output-token count is known gen_ai.server.ttft Histogram seconds Superseded spelling of TTFT gen_ai.server.tbt Histogram seconds Time between streamed chunks: one sample per stream, its mean gap. With GENAI_METRICS_PROFILE=full, one sample per gap

docs.title: Token Usage Metrics
docs.text:
semantic-conventions-genai#374 replaced the gen_ai.client.token.usage histogram and its gen_ai.token.type attribute with these instruments. They are recorded for every inference call whose provider reported usage.

Metric Type Unit Records gen_ai.client.inference.usage.input_tokens Counter {token} Input tokens, cached ones included gen_ai.client.inference.usage.output_tokens Counter {token} Output tokens, reasoning ones included gen_ai.client.inference.usage.cache_read.input_tokens Counter {token} Input tokens served from the provider's cache. Part of input_tokens gen_ai.client.inference.usage.cache_write.input_tokens Counter {token} Input tokens written to the provider's cache. Part of input_tokens gen_ai.client.inference.usage.reasoning.output_tokens Counter {token} Output tokens spent on reasoning. Part of output_tokens gen_ai.client.inference.operation.input_tokens Histogram {token} One call's input tokens gen_ai.client.inference.operation.output_tokens Histogram {token} One call's output tokens

Attributes, each only when the span has it: gen_ai.operation.name, gen_ai.provider.name (read from gen_ai.system when only that is set), gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.response.model, server.address, server.port. The counters also carry gen_ai.token.modality; the histograms do not, because percentiles taken per modality do not add up to a call.

  • Modality. Where the provider breaks usage down (text, image, audio), each part is counted under its modality and whatever the breakdown leaves over is counted under unknown, so the modalities of one counter always add up to its total. Usage with no breakdown is all unknown.
  • Zero and missing counts record nothing on the counters, as semantic-conventions-genai#602 proposes: a call with no cache activity adds no cache_read point. The histograms record one value per call whenever usage was reported, zero included.
  • Agent runs. When a framework span (an agent, crew, graph or workflow run) is the one that accounts a run's tokens, they are added to the counters but not to the histograms: a run's total is not the size of any one model call.
  • Cached input is counted as input. Anthropic reports input_tokens without its cache reads and writes; the input counter adds them back so that the cache counters stay subsets of it. The gen_ai.usage.input_tokens span attribute is unchanged.
  • Not recorded: embeddings calls (the conventions are to give them their own instrument), token counts this library estimated because the provider returned none (they stay on the span, marked gen_ai.usage.token_count_estimated, and on gen_ai.client.token.usage), and failed calls.

gen_ai.client.token.usage is still recorded alongside these with its existing token_type label, so dashboards built on it keep working. It is removed at 2.0.

docs.title: Evaluation Runtime Attributes
docs.text:
Written on a span by the evaluation runtime, whichever detectors are enabled.

Attribute Type Description evaluation.completed boolean The detectors ran for this span evaluation.skipped string Why they did not: overloaded (the queue was full) or shutdown (the process was exiting) evaluation.truncated boolean Detectors read only part of the prompt or response evaluation.prompt.length int Characters in the prompt, when it was cut evaluation.prompt.analyzed_length int Characters of it the detectors read evaluation.response.length int Characters in the response, when it was cut evaluation.response.analyzed_length int Characters of it the detectors read evaluation.pii.prompt.pattern_analyzed_length int Characters the PII patterns covered evaluation.pii.prompt.model_analyzed_length int Characters the PII entity model read evaluation.<detector>.prompt.analyzed_length int Characters read by prompt_injection, restricted_topics or bias when it has a block policy: the whole prompt

docs.title: A2A (Agent2Agent)
docs.text:
a2a.* keys follow the OpenTelemetry A2A conventions (development status); the part and artifact counts are genai_otel additions. a2a.protocol.binding is provisional while OpenTelemetry settles how to record the binding. Content rules and error mapping: A2A.

Attribute Type Notes a2a.method.name string SendMessage, SendStreamingMessage, GetTask, ... a2a.protocol.version, a2a.protocol.binding (provisional), a2a.tenant string binding is jsonrpc, grpc or http_json a2a.message.id, a2a.message.reference_task_ids, a2a.task.id, a2a.task.state string / string[] state is lower-case, e.g. input_required a2a.message.{text,file,data}_part_count, a2a.response.{text,file,data}_part_count, a2a.artifact.count, a2a.agent.skill_count int counts only (genai_otel) a2a.message.file_media_types, a2a.response.file_media_types string[] media types of file parts; never their bytes, URLs or names a2a.message.text, a2a.message.data, a2a.response.text, a2a.response.data, a2a.agent.skill_names string / string[] only with content capture on

Also set: gen_ai.conversation.id (the A2A contextId), gen_ai.agent.name / .description / .version (from the Agent Card), gen_ai.operation.name=invoke_agent (client spans), error.type, server.address, server.port.

docs.title: A2UI (Agent-to-UI)
docs.text:
OpenTelemetry has no convention for A2UI, and the protocol defines no telemetry, so every a2ui.* key is a provisional genai_otel addition that may be renamed if a convention settles on other names. They appear on A2A spans that carry A2UI parts and on the a2ui.parse_response, a2ui.parse_stream and a2ui.process {type} spans. Content rules: A2UI.

Attribute Type Notes a2ui.protocol.version string 1.0, 0.9 or 0.8; left off when the operation saw more than one a2ui.agent_message.count, a2ui.renderer_message.count int Messages the agent sent to the renderer, and the renderer sent to the agent a2ui.message.types string[] Sorted distinct types: create_surface, update_components, update_data_model, delete_surface, call_renderer_function, agent_function_response, action, call_agent_function, renderer_function_response, error a2ui.surface.id, a2ui.surface.count string / int The surface when single; the distinct count a2ui.catalog.id, a2ui.catalog.ids string / string[] The catalog when single; every catalog referenced a2ui.component.count int Components in createSurface and updateComponents messages a2ui.renderer.supported_catalog_ids string[] From the renderer's capabilities metadata a2ui.action.name, a2ui.function.name string The user action's name, or the function called, when single a2ui.error.codes, a2ui.error.count string[] / int Renderer and function error codes (VALIDATION_FAILED, UNALLOWED_PARENT, EXECUTION_ERROR, ...) and how many a2ui.validation.outcome string valid or invalid, from agent-side parsing a2ui.extension.active bool The A2UI A2A extension URI was among the call's extensions (set only when true) a2ui.messages, a2ui.data_model, a2ui.action.context, a2ui.error.paths, a2ui.error.messages, a2ui.component.types string / string[] only with content capture on; media URLs inside components are never recorded

Each renderer error or function error is also a span event a2ui.error with a2ui.error.code and a2ui.surface.id. error.type is reused for a parse or validation failure.

docs.title: Object storage (S3 API and SeaweedFS)

docs.title: Server Metrics - Manual Instrumentation Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how to use the Server Metrics Collector for manual instrumentation of server-side LLM serving metrics, including KV cache usage and request queue depth.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Server metrics are designed for production LLM serving scenarios where you have access to server-side statistics from frameworks like: - Ollama - Local LLM serving with automatic metrics collection (see Automatic Integration section) - vLLM - High-throughput LLM serving - TGI (Text Generation Inference) - HuggingFace's serving solution - Custom serving infrastructure - Your own LLM servers

These metrics complement the automatic client-side instrumentation and provide insights into server capacity, memory usage, and request processing.

Note: Ollama integration is automatic - no manual instrumentation needed! See the Ollama Automatic Integration section below.

docs.title: KV Cache Metrics
docs.text: gen_ai.server.kv_cache.usage (Gauge) - GPU KV-cache usage percentage (0-100) - Attributes: model (model name) - Use case: Monitor memory pressure, detect cache exhaustion

docs.title: Request Queue Metrics
docs.text:
gen_ai.server.requests.running (Gauge) - Number of requests currently executing on GPU - Use case: Track active request load

gen_ai.server.requests.waiting (Gauge) - Number of requests queued for processing - Use case: Detect request queueing, identify bottlenecks

gen_ai.server.requests.max (Gauge) - Maximum concurrent request capacity - Use case: Track capacity limits, plan scaling

docs.title: 1. Initialize Instrumentation
docs.text:
import genai_otel

# Initialize with automatic instrumentation
genai_otel.instrument()

# Get the server metrics collector
server_metrics = genai_otel.get_server_metrics()

docs.title: 2. Set KV Cache Usage
docs.text:
# Update KV cache usage for a model (0-100%)
server_metrics.set_kv_cache_usage("gpt-4", 75.5)
server_metrics.set_kv_cache_usage("llama-2-70b", 42.0)

docs.title: 3. Track Request Queue
docs.text:
# Set maximum capacity
server_metrics.set_requests_max(50)

# Update current state
server_metrics.set_requests_running(5)   # 5 active requests
server_metrics.set_requests_waiting(12)  # 12 queued requests

docs.title: 4. Use Increment/Decrement Helpers
docs.text:
# When a request starts
server_metrics.increment_requests_running()

# When a request completes
server_metrics.decrement_requests_running()

# For queue management
server_metrics.increment_requests_waiting()
server_metrics.decrement_requests_waiting()

docs.title: Ollama Automatic Integration
docs.text:
Ollama server metrics are collected automatically - no manual instrumentation required!

Note: This feature requires Python 3.11 or higher. On Python 3.9 and 3.10, the feature is automatically skipped and a debug message is logged. Basic Ollama instrumentation (tracing and metrics) still works on all supported Python versions.

When you enable Ollama instrumentation, the library automatically: 1. Polls Ollama's /api/ps endpoint every 5 seconds (configurable) 2. Extracts VRAM usage per model 3. Updates gen_ai.server.kv_cache.usage metrics 4. Tracks number of models loaded in memory

docs.title: Quick Start with Ollama
docs.text:
import genai_otel

# Initialize instrumentation (Ollama server metrics enabled by default)
genai_otel.instrument()

import ollama

# Make requests - metrics are collected automatically in the background
response = ollama.generate(model="llama2", prompt="Hello!")

That's it! The metrics will appear automatically.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Control Ollama server metrics via environment variables:

# Enable/disable automatic Ollama server metrics (default: true)
export GENAI_ENABLE_OLLAMA_SERVER_METRICS=true

# Ollama server URL (default: http://localhost:11434)
export OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434

# Polling interval in seconds (default: 5.0)
export GENAI_OLLAMA_METRICS_INTERVAL=5.0

# OPTIONAL: Your GPU's VRAM in GB for accurate percentage calculation
# If not set, VRAM is auto-detected using nvidia-ml-py or nvidia-smi
# Only set this if auto-detection fails or you want to override
# Example: 24 for RTX 4090, 16 for RTX 4080, 12 for RTX 3080
# export GENAI_OLLAMA_MAX_VRAM_GB=24

GPU VRAM Auto-Detection: The poller automatically detects your GPU's VRAM using: 1. nvidia-ml-py (preferred) - Requires pip install genai-otel-instrument[gpu] 2. nvidia-smi (fallback) - Uses the command-line tool if available 3. Manual override - Set GENAI_OLLAMA_MAX_VRAM_GB to bypass auto-detection

Auto-detection logs: 

INFO - Auto-detected GPU VRAM: 24.0GB  # Success via nvidia-ml-py
INFO - Auto-detected GPU VRAM: 16.0GB  # Success via nvidia-smi
INFO - GPU VRAM not detected, using heuristic-based percentages  # Both failed

docs.title: What Gets Collected
docs.text:
The automatic poller queries /api/ps and collects:

Per-Model Metrics: - gen_ai.server.kv_cache.usage{model="llama2"} - VRAM usage percentage - Calculated from model's size_vram field

Example Output: 

{
  "name": "gen_ai.server.kv_cache.usage",
  "description": "GPU KV-cache usage percentage",
  "unit": "%",
  "data": {
    "attributes": {"model": "llama2:latest"},
    "value": 45.2
  }
}

docs.title: Disabling Automatic Collection
docs.text:
To disable (and use manual instrumentation instead):

export GENAI_ENABLE_OLLAMA_SERVER_METRICS=false

docs.title: Example with Configuration
docs.text:
See examples/ollama/example_with_server_metrics.py for a complete demonstration.

import os
import genai_otel

# Configure before instrumentation
os.environ["GENAI_OLLAMA_METRICS_INTERVAL"] = "3.0"  # Poll every 3 seconds
os.environ["GENAI_OLLAMA_MAX_VRAM_GB"] = "24"  # 24GB GPU

genai_otel.instrument()

import ollama

# Use Ollama normally - metrics collected automatically
response = ollama.chat(
    model="llama2",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
)

# Check what metrics were collected
from genai_otel import get_server_metrics
server_metrics = get_server_metrics()

# View KV cache usage
for model, usage in server_metrics._kv_cache_usage.items():
    print(f"{model}: {usage:.2f}% VRAM")

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
The OllamaServerMetricsPoller: 1. Runs in a background daemon thread 2. Queries http://localhost:11434/api/ps every N seconds 3. Parses the JSON response to extract model VRAM usage 4. Calculates percentage based on either: - GENAI_OLLAMA_MAX_VRAM_GB (if configured) - accurate percentage - Model size heuristic (if not configured) - approximation 5. Updates the global ServerMetricsCollector instance

The poller gracefully handles: - Ollama server not running (logs debug message) - Connection timeouts (2 second timeout per request) - Parse errors (logs warnings) - No models loaded (metrics show 0)

docs.title: vLLM Integration
docs.text:
from vllm import AsyncLLMEngine
import asyncio
import genai_otel

genai_otel.instrument()
server_metrics = genai_otel.get_server_metrics()

async def update_server_metrics(engine: AsyncLLMEngine):
    """Periodically update server metrics from vLLM engine."""
    while True:
        try:
            # Get KV cache statistics
            for model_name in engine.model_names:
                cache_stats = await engine.get_model_cache_stats(model_name)
                cache_usage_pct = (
                    cache_stats["used_blocks"] / cache_stats["total_blocks"]
                ) * 100
                server_metrics.set_kv_cache_usage(model_name, cache_usage_pct)

            # Get request queue statistics
            queue_stats = await engine.get_request_queue_stats()
            server_metrics.set_requests_running(queue_stats["running"])
            server_metrics.set_requests_waiting(queue_stats["waiting"])

        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error updating metrics: {e}")

        await asyncio.sleep(1)  # Update every second

# Start metrics updater as background task
asyncio.create_task(update_server_metrics(engine))

docs.title: TGI (Text Generation Inference) Integration
docs.text:
import requests
import genai_otel
from threading import Thread
import time

genai_otel.instrument()
server_metrics = genai_otel.get_server_metrics()

def poll_tgi_metrics(tgi_metrics_url: str, interval: float = 1.0):
    """Poll TGI metrics endpoint and update server metrics."""
    while True:
        try:
            response = requests.get(f"{tgi_metrics_url}/metrics")
            metrics = parse_prometheus_metrics(response.text)

            # Extract relevant metrics (adjust based on TGI version)
            server_metrics.set_requests_running(
                metrics.get("tgi_request_inference_count", 0)
            )
            server_metrics.set_requests_waiting(
                metrics.get("tgi_queue_size", 0)
            )

        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error polling TGI metrics: {e}")

        time.sleep(interval)

# Start metrics poller in background thread
Thread(target=poll_tgi_metrics, args=("http://localhost:8080",), daemon=True).start()

docs.title: Custom Request Handler Integration
docs.text:
import genai_otel
from contextlib import contextmanager

genai_otel.instrument()
server_metrics = genai_otel.get_server_metrics()

@contextmanager
def track_request():
    """Context manager to track request lifecycle."""
    server_metrics.increment_requests_running()
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        server_metrics.decrement_requests_running()

class LLMRequestHandler:
    def __init__(self):
        # Set max capacity
        server_metrics.set_requests_max(100)

    async def handle_request(self, request):
        # Track request processing
        with track_request():
            # Your request processing logic
            result = await self.process_llm_request(request)
            return result

    def update_cache_metrics(self, model: str, cache_usage: float):
        """Update KV cache metrics (called from your cache manager)."""
        server_metrics.set_kv_cache_usage(model, cache_usage)

docs.title: Thread Safety
docs.text:
All server metrics operations are thread-safe and can be called from: - Multiple threads - Async coroutines - Background workers - Request handlers

The ServerMetricsCollector uses internal locks to ensure atomic updates.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Update Frequency: Update KV cache metrics every 1-5 seconds for accurate monitoring
  2. Request Tracking: Use increment/decrement methods in try-finally blocks
  3. Model Names: Use consistent model naming across your stack
  4. Capacity Planning: Set requests_max based on your GPU memory and model size
  5. Alerting: Set up alerts for high cache usage (>90%) and queue depth

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Metrics not appearing in Prometheus: - Ensure genai_otel.instrument() is called before using metrics - Check OTLP endpoint configuration - Verify metrics are being set (use debug logging)

KV cache always shows 0: - Server metrics require manual instrumentation - Must call set_kv_cache_usage() explicitly - Check integration with your serving framework

Request counts incorrect: - Use try-finally to ensure decrements always happen - Check for exceptions in request handlers - Verify no requests are bypassing tracking
