docs.title: A2A (Agent2Agent) instrumentation (spec)
docs.text: Status: APPROVED 2026-11-12. A2A-D1 to A2A-D7 are approved as recommended. It ships in 1.47.0, together with SeaweedFS and the Gemini Decisions API.

docs.title: 1. Problem
docs.text:
A2A reached 1.0 and moved to the Linux Foundation. It is the cross-vendor protocol agents use to discover one another (the Agent Card), negotiate modalities, run tasks together and exchange messages, without exposing their internals. This library records nothing A2A-specific today: no module, test or document mentions it.

The official Python SDK, a2a-sdk (1.3.0, 2026-10-27; spec 1.0 with a 0.3 compatibility mode), already makes spans of its own through a2a.utils.telemetry.trace_class. These are on by default whenever OpenTelemetry is installed, and OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_A2A_SDK_ENABLED=false turns them off. Reading the 1.3.0 source:

  • Generic spans. Spans are named <module>.<Class>.<method> and carry no A2A attributes: no method, task, context, message or agent.
  • Wrong span kinds on internal plumbing. Internal classes are marked SpanKind.SERVER: the event queues, the event consumer and the in-memory queue manager. The client transports (JSON-RPC, REST, gRPC) are CLIENT, and the request handlers and dispatchers are SERVER. One request therefore produces many SERVER spans, so a backend that counts SERVER spans as requests over-counts.
  • No trace propagation between agents. No module calls opentelemetry.propagate.inject or extract, or mentions traceparent. A call from agent A to agent B therefore starts a new trace in B unless an HTTP or gRPC instrumentation happens to carry the context. This is the gap described in A2A issue #2103.

OpenTelemetry merged A2A semantic conventions on 2026-10-27 (semantic-conventions-genai PR #195, development status). Still open:

  • metrics (PR #651);
  • how to record which binding (JSON-RPC, gRPC or HTTP+JSON) carried a call (issue #612).

docs.title: 2. The conventions we follow (PR #195)
docs.text:
• a2a.client (CLIENT) is one logical client operation, including consuming a response stream.
  • a2a.server (SERVER) is used only when no transport server span exists. Otherwise the A2A attributes enrich the existing HTTP or gRPC server span instead of nesting a new one.
  • Span name: {a2a.method.name} {target}.
  • A2A attributes:
  • a2a.method.name;
  • a2a.protocol.version;
  • a2a.tenant;
  • a2a.message.id;
  • a2a.message.reference_task_ids;
  • a2a.task.id;
  • a2a.task.state.
  • Reused attributes:
  • gen_ai.conversation.id holds the A2A contextId;
  • gen_ai.agent.name, gen_ai.agent.description and gen_ai.agent.version come from the Agent Card;
  • error.type, server.address and server.port.
  • Multi-valued attributes: a task or conversation attribute is omitted when one operation saw several distinct values, for example task states across stream events.

docs.title: 3. Proposal
docs.text:
1. New instrumentor a2a, which follows the mcp_semconv layout. It is a no-op when a2a-sdk is not installed or is older than 1.0. The 0.3 compatibility transports are covered only where they share the 1.x client and handler classes.
  2. Client side. Wrap the a2a.client.Client / BaseClient operations:
  3. send_message, including streaming;
  4. get_task, list_tasks and cancel_task;
  5. subscribe;
  6. the push-notification config calls;
  7. get_extended_agent_card.

Each call emits one a2a.client span, and a streaming call ends the span when the stream ends. Attributes come from the request, the response and the resolved Agent Card. server.address and server.port come from the card URL. 3. Server side. Wrap the request handler (DefaultRequestHandler, v1 and v2, and the gRPC handler). - When a transport server span is current (the FastAPI, Starlette, ASGI or gRPC instrumentation), add the A2A attributes to it and rename it to {a2a.method.name} {target} per the convention, for HTTP only. - Otherwise open one a2a.server span. 4. Trace propagation between agents. - The client injects W3C traceparent / tracestate and baggage through the SDK's own interceptor hook (ClientCallInterceptor). For HTTP it uses headers; for gRPC, metadata. - The server extracts them when no transport instrumentation has already done so. - The result: agent A's call and agent B's work are one trace. GENAI_A2A_PROPAGATE=false turns this off. 5. The SDK's own spans. When our instrumentor is active and the user has not set OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_A2A_SDK_ENABLED, we set it to false before a2a is imported. This stops the generic and mis-kinded spans from doubling every operation. A user who sets the variable keeps their choice. This is decision A2A-D2. 6. Binding (issue #612). Record the binding under a provisional name, a2a.protocol.binding (jsonrpc, grpc or http_json), marked provisional in the docs. If the convention settles on another name or on derivation, we follow it in a later release. This is decision A2A-D3. 7. Content. The existing content-capture rule applies. - Always recorded (not content): the method; task, message and context ids; the task state; the counts of message parts by kind (text, file, data); the artifact count; and the Agent Card name, description and version. - Recorded only with content capture on: message and artifact text, and data parts. Files are never inlined; they are counted and typed only. - Card skills: recorded by count, with names under content capture, because skill names can describe business processes. This is decision A2A-D4. 8. Errors. A JSON-RPC error, gRPC status or HTTP error sets the span to ERROR with error.type. The type is the A2A error name where one exists (for example TaskNotFoundError), otherwise the status code. A task that ends in failed or rejected sets a2a.task.state but does not on its own mark the span ERROR: the call succeeded and the agent's answer was a refusal or a failure. This is decision A2A-D5. 9. Agent graph. The a2a.client span gets gen_ai.operation.name = invoke_agent and the target agent's gen_ai.agent.name. Backends can then draw an edge from the calling agent to the called agent. That makes A2A calls visible in agent graphs, not only in waterfalls. 10. Metrics. None in this release. They follow PR #651 when it merges, so we don't publish names that change. 11. Tests. No network and no real servers are needed; fakes and the a2a-sdk test helpers are used where installed (importorskip). Cover: - client send, including streaming, get and cancel; - server enrichment of an existing span, and a standalone a2a.server span; - propagation round trip, with one trace across client and server; - OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_A2A_SDK_ENABLED respected when the user has set it, and defaulted otherwise; - content capture off and on; - error mapping; - failed-task semantics; - no-op without a2a-sdk.

docs.title: 4. Decisions for approval
docs.text: Question Recommendation A2A-D1 Instrument the official Python a2a-sdk (1.x) only in this release Yes. The Java, Go, JavaScript and .NET ports follow their own pins A2A-D2 Turn off a2a-sdk's own generic spans by default when ours are active, unless the user set the variable Yes. They double every operation and mark queue internals as SERVER A2A-D3 Record the binding as provisional a2a.protocol.binding while issue #612 is open Yes, marked provisional A2A-D4 Content rule: ids, states, counts and card identity always; text, data and skill names only under content capture; files never inlined Yes A2A-D5 A failed or rejected task is not by itself an ERROR span Yes. The call worked; the agent said no A2A-D6 Propagate trace context between agents by default, with GENAI_A2A_PROPAGATE=false to opt out Yes. This is the main value: one trace across agents A2A-D7 Ship in 1.47.0 with SeaweedFS and the Gemini Decisions API Yes, per the founder

docs.title: 5. Out of scope
docs.text:
• A2A metrics (PR #651) and an upstream proposal for the binding attribute, which belongs to the convention.
  • Non-Python A2A SDKs.
  • Agent Card signature or authentication details, which are not recorded.

docs.title: 6. Implementation notes and deviations (1.47.0)
docs.text:
Code: genai_otel/a2a_semconv/ (attributes.py, extract.py, instrumentor.py); registered as a2a in INSTRUMENTORS and in DEFAULT_INSTRUMENTORS; setting a2a_propagate (GENAI_A2A_PROPAGATE). Tests: tests/a2a_semconv/, against the real a2a-sdk 1.3.0 over an in-process ASGI app (the client's httpx transport runs the server in an empty context, so only the propagated header can join the two sides). The SDK is in the dev extra and the tests importorskip it.

What is wrapped, checked against the 1.3.0 source:

  • Client: a2a.client.base_client.BaseClient: send_message, subscribe (async generators), get_task, list_tasks, cancel_task, create_task_push_notification_config, get_task_push_notification_config, list_task_push_notification_configs, delete_task_push_notification_config, get_extended_agent_card. Client itself is abstract. Propagation is an a2a.client.interceptors.ClientCallInterceptor whose before() merges the W3C headers into ClientCallContext.service_parameters, which the SDK turns into HTTP headers (http_helpers.get_http_args) and gRPC metadata (GrpcTransport._get_grpc_metadata).
  • Server: DefaultRequestHandlerV2 (DefaultRequestHandler is an alias of it) and LegacyRequestHandler: on_message_send, on_message_send_stream, on_get_task, on_list_tasks, on_cancel_task, the three push-config methods that exist plus on_delete_task_push_notification_config, on_subscribe_to_task, on_get_extended_agent_card. GrpcHandler and both HTTP dispatchers call these, so all three bindings are covered by one wrapper. The binding on a server span comes from ServerCallContext.state (grpc_context / method / headers).

Deviations and choices the spec left open:

  1. Span names. Spans are named {a2a.method.name} {target} per section 2, for both client and server. a2a.client / a2a.server are the convention's names for the two kinds of span, not literal span names. The instrumentation scope is genai_otel.a2a.
  2. Baggage goes through the existing session-baggage policy (SessionBaggagePropagator), not a blanket W3C baggage inject: baggage crosses a trust boundary here, and session.id / user.id leave only when named in GENAI_SESSION_BAGGAGE_KEYS and are accepted only when named in GENAI_SESSION_BAGGAGE_ACCEPT. Other baggage passes as the stock propagator would. Trace context uses the explicit W3C propagators, not whatever the global propagator is.
  3. Attribute names the spec left open (all a2a.*, marked as genai_otel additions in the docs): a2a.message.{text,file,data}_part_count, a2a.response.{text,file,data}_part_count, a2a.artifact.count, a2a.agent.skill_count, a2a.message.file_media_types, a2a.response.file_media_types; content keys a2a.message.text, a2a.message.data, a2a.response.text, a2a.response.data, a2a.agent.skill_names. File media types are recorded without content capture (they are type, not content); file bytes, URLs and names never.
  4. Task state values are lower-case without the proto prefix (input_required).
  5. A stream records its final task state (founder decision, 2026-11-12). A normal stream passes through submitted, working and completed, and a2a.task.state is the last state seen, provided the operation concerned at most one task. This departs from the convention's literal multi-valued rule, on purpose. Task id and context id are still omitted when they have several values.
  6. Enabled by default (in DEFAULT_INSTRUMENTORS), since it is a no-op without a2a-sdk 1.x.
  7. The propagation interceptor is attached on the first call of each client (so clients built before instrument() are covered), not by wrapping BaseClient.__init__. It edits a copy of the caller's ClientCallContext, never the caller's object.
  8. The SDK's own spans. a2a.utils.telemetry reads OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_A2A_SDK_ENABLED once at import and swaps its tracer for a no-op. We set the default only while that module is not yet in sys.modules; when it is and its spans are on, one INFO line says so and nothing is hacked (the module's trace global could be patched, and is deliberately not). In that mode the SDK's SERVER spans are recognised by their scope (a2a-python-sdk) and are never mistaken for the transport span; trace-context extraction on the server then needs transport instrumentation, because the SDK's span is already current.
  9. Packaging. genai_otel.a2a_semconv was added to [tool.setuptools] packages. genai_otel.mcp_semconv (and genai_otel.voice) are not in that list; that predates this change and was left alone, but it should be checked before the release is built.

Not verified: gRPC end to end (no server is started; the metadata read, the binding and the no-rename rule are tested against a stand-in ServicerContext, and the interceptor's output is the same service_parameters the SDK's gRPC transport turns into metadata); a2a-sdk versions other than 1.3.0; the 0.3 compatibility transports beyond the class-name binding match; a client built on Client subclasses other than BaseClient.

docs.title: A2UI (Agent-to-UI) instrumentation (spec)
docs.text: Status: APPROVED 2026-11-12. A2UI-D1 to A2UI-D11 are approved as recommended. The Python part ships in 1.48.0. The Node part covers Node, browser and React Native applications and ships as the next npm release of @traceverse/genai-otel-instrument-node (after 0.1.0-alpha.10). Correction 2026-11-12: the Node port is published on npm, so it gets a release too; its contract is pinned to v1.46.0, not v1.30.0.

docs.title: 1. Problem
docs.text:
A2UI is Google's open protocol (Apache 2.0) for an agent to send a user interface as declarative JSON instead of code. The agent describes surfaces and components from a catalog the client trusts. The client draws them with its own native components (React, Lit, Angular, Flutter, SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose). The client sends user actions back to the agent. v1.0 is the current protocol version on a2ui.org; v0.9.1 and v0.9 are previous, and v0.8 is deprecated.

This library records nothing A2UI-specific today. A2UI usually travels inside A2A messages, so 1.47.0's A2A spans see it, but only as an anonymous data part: the span cannot say that a UI was sent, which surface or catalog it used, what the user did with it, or that the client rejected it. The protocol defines no telemetry of its own.

What matters for observability, in order:

  1. The agent produced UI the client rejected. Renderer error messages (VALIDATION_FAILED, UNALLOWED_PARENT, UNALLOWED_CHILD, function errors) mean the user saw a broken or missing interface while every server-side span looked healthy.
  2. The model produced UI the agent SDK could not parse or validate. The agent SDK drops the response, so the user sees nothing. This is a model-quality signal: invalid output from the LLM.
  3. What the user did. An action message is the user's click or submit. It starts the agent's next turn and belongs in the same trace as the UI that offered it.
  4. What was shown. The surface, the catalog, the protocol version and the size of the update.

docs.title: 2. The protocol, as read from the sources
docs.text:
Sources: the v1.0 specification and the A2A extension specification on a2ui.org, and the Python packages a2ui-agent-sdk 0.11.0, a2ui-a2a 0.3.0 and a2ui-core 0.6.0 (all read from their published wheels).

  • Agent-to-renderer messages. Each message has exactly one of createSurface, updateComponents, updateDataModel, deleteSurface, callRendererFunction or agentFunctionResponse, and a top-level "version": "1.0". v0.9 messages have the same shape with their own version; v0.8 messages have no version.
  • Renderer-to-agent messages. Each has exactly one of action, callAgentFunction, rendererFunctionResponse or error.
  • Identity. surfaceId on surface messages. catalogId on createSurface (the surface default), @catalogId on a component that overrides it, and catalogId on function calls. These are string identifiers, not URLs.
  • Errors. A validation error is {"error": {"code", "surfaceId", "path", "message"}}. Function responses carry error.code and error.message (INVALID_FUNCTION_CALL, EXECUTION_ERROR, EXPRESSION_ERROR, INTEGRITY_ERROR).
  • Over A2A.
  • The extension URI is https://a2ui.org/a2a-extension/a2ui/v1.0. It is activated through the X-A2A-Extensions header (JSON-RPC and HTTP) or the gRPC metadata["X-A2A-Extensions"]. Activation is optional.
  • An A2UI part is a DataPart whose metadata["mimeType"] is application/a2ui+json. v0.8 and v0.9 use the deprecated application/json+a2ui, and receivers must accept both.
  • The spec and the SDK disagree on the part payload. The spec says the data field MUST be an array of messages, processed in order and not as a transaction. The Python SDK writes one message per DataPart (create_a2ui_part). Both shapes must be read.
  • The renderer advertises its catalogs in message.metadata["a2uiRendererCapabilities"]["1.0"]["supportedCatalogIds"]. The Python SDK's constant is a2uiClientCapabilities, and both keys must be read.
  • Other transports. The agent SDK also integrates with Google ADK and MCP, and leaves the transport to the application.
  • A version trap. a2ui-a2a 0.3.0 requires a2a-sdk>=0.3.0,<0.4.0. 1.47.0's A2A instrumentor covers a2a-sdk 1.x only and is a no-op on 0.3. An agent built on the official A2UI-over-A2A bridge therefore gets no A2A spans today, so A2UI coverage cannot depend on the A2A instrumentor alone.

docs.title: 2.1 The SDKs a2ui.org lists, and what covers each
docs.text: Listed SDK Side Covered by a2ui-agent-sdk (PyPI, 0.11.0; protocol v0.8, v0.9.1, v1.0) Agent 3.2 a2ui-a2a (PyPI, 0.3.0; pins a2a-sdk 0.3) Agent, A2A bridge 3.2 (its parts come from the agent SDK). 3.1 does not apply, because that needs A2A 1.x (A2UI-D2) a2ui-adk (PyPI, 0.3.0; Google ADK) Agent 3.2 (it calls the agent SDK's processor) @a2ui/agent (npm, 0.1.0, 2026-11-02; the TypeScript port of the agent SDK, same A2uiRequestProcessor / Parser surface) Agent, Node 4.0 @a2ui/web_core (npm, 0.15.0) with @a2ui/react, @a2ui/lit, @a2ui/angular Renderer, web 4.3, plus 4.1 and 4.2 for the transport a2ui_agent (Dart) and Flutter Agent and renderer Out of scope: no Dart port SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose renderers, legacy Kotlin agent SDK Renderer / agent Out of scope: no Swift port. The Java port has no A2A or A2UI support (a later spec) Go community libraries (satorunooshie/a2ui-go, tmc/a2ui) and terminal renderers Agent / renderer A2UI-D9

docs.title: 3.1 Recognise A2UI inside A2A spans (a2a-sdk 1.x)
docs.text:
Extend genai_otel/a2a_semconv/extract.py. When a data part carries either A2UI media type (in metadata["mimeType"] or in the part's media_type), parse its payload as an A2UI message or list of messages and add the a2ui.* attributes of section 5 to the existing A2A span:

  • the request side for what the renderer sent;
  • the response side, including stream events and artifacts, for what the agent sent.

This needs no new span. A2UI parts still count in the A2A data part counts, unchanged. The extension URI in X-A2A-Extensions, when present, sets a2ui.extension.active=true.

docs.title: 3.2 Instrument the agent SDK (a2ui-agent-sdk, any transport)
docs.text:
This works whether the agent speaks A2A 0.3, A2A 1.x, ADK, MCP or something else.

  • A2uiRequestProcessor.parse_response gets one INTERNAL span, a2ui.parse_response. It records the messages produced and their attributes.
  • If parsing or validation raises, the span is ERROR with error.type set to the exception class.
  • a2ui.validation.outcome is valid or invalid.
  • Under the active LLM span when there is one, this is where "the model wrote broken UI" becomes visible.
  • A2uiRequestProcessor.open_stream gets one span, a2ui.parse_stream, which covers the whole stream. Its attributes are the totals at the end.
  • RendererToAgentMessageProcessor.process_message gets one INTERNAL span, a2ui.process {message type} (for example a2ui.process action). It records:
  • the incoming message's attributes;
  • the reply count;
  • renderer error messages, by code.
  • parse_content_to_parts catches every exception and logs only its class. Our wrapper records it as a2ui.validation.outcome=invalid on the current span. It changes neither the return value nor the logging.

No-op when a2ui-agent-sdk is not installed or is older than 0.11. Protocol versions v1.0 and v0.9 are read; v0.8 is recognised by media type and counted, but its message shapes are not parsed (it is deprecated).

docs.title: 3.3 What is not instrumented in Python
docs.text:
• No renderer. Python has no A2UI renderer.
  • The prompt-building parts of the agent SDK (schema prompts, catalog pruning, examples). They run before the LLM call and the LLM span already records the prompt under content capture.

docs.title: 4. Proposal: Node, browser and React Native
docs.text: The Node SDK is the port for Node services, browsers and React Native apps. In a mobile or web app the app is the renderer: it receives the agent's UI and sends the user's actions. Three pieces are needed.

docs.title: 4.0 The TypeScript agent SDK (@a2ui/agent)
docs.text:
@a2ui/agent 0.1.0 is the TypeScript port of the Python agent SDK. It exports the same A2uiRequestProcessor, Parser and response-stream classes, and its error classes (A2uiValidationError, ParseError, the Express* errors). An agent written in Node gets the same spans as section 3.2:

  • a2ui.parse_response;
  • a2ui.parse_stream, which is ERROR on a parse or validation failure, with error.type set to the error class.

The exact method names are checked against the 0.1.0 sources at implementation time. 0.1.0 exports no renderer-to-agent processor, so the a2ui.process span is Python-only until the TypeScript SDK adds one. The Node agent's A2A server spans remain A2UI-D6.

docs.title: 4.1 A2A client instrumentation for @a2a-js/sdk (prerequisite)
docs.text:
The Node SDK has no A2A support today. A renderer talks to its agent over A2A, so without this there is no span for the call, no A2UI attributes on it, and no trace from the user's tap to the agent's work.

  • Port the client half of the 1.47.0 Python design to @a2a-js/sdk 1.x: a2a.client spans, the same attributes, W3C trace-context injection through the SDK's interceptor or fetch hook, and the same content rule.
  • The server half (a Node agent) is in scope only if A2UI-D6 says so.

docs.title: 4.2 Wire-level A2UI recognition, independent of the renderer
docs.text:
The renderer landscape is fragmented. The official ones are React, Lit and Angular (sharing @a2ui/web_core), plus Flutter, SwiftUI and Compose. Community ones include two React Native renderers (a2ui-react-native-renderer 1.0.0 on npm for v1.0, and sivamrudram-eng/a2ui-react-native for v0.8), Vue, Svelte, Lynx and terminal renderers. Patching each renderer does not scale. Instead:

  • A2A client spans parse A2UI parts the same way as section 3.1. On the request, they record the user action being sent and the renderer capabilities. On the response, they record what the agent sent. This alone covers any renderer that talks to its agent through @a2a-js/sdk.
  • A small public API for apps whose transport we do not see (AG-UI, a custom WebSocket, MCP Apps): recordA2uiReceived(messages), recordA2uiSent(message) and recordA2uiRendererError(error). Each adds the attributes of section 5 to the current span, or opens a short INTERNAL span when none is active. All three are exported from the Node, browser and React Native entry points.

docs.title: 4.3 Renderer adapter for @a2ui/web_core (official web renderers)
docs.text:
@a2ui/react, @a2ui/lit and @a2ui/angular share @a2ui/web_core (0.15). An opt-in adapter wraps its message processor:

  • it records one a2ui.apply span per batch of agent messages applied, with the duration until the batch is processed;
  • it records renderer-side validation errors as span events with their code, even when the app never sends the error message back to the agent.

The community React Native renderers do not depend on web_core. For them the A2A path in 4.1 and 4.2 and the API in 4.2 apply. A dedicated adapter for a2ui-react-native-renderer is decision A2UI-D7.

docs.title: 4.4 Porting rule
docs.text: The Node port vendors the Python contract (semantic conventions, configuration, pricing) from one pinned Python tag, with SHA checks, and its parity matrix tracks every difference. The A2UI and A2A attribute names are added to the vendored contract from the 1.48.0 tag, not typed in by hand. Re-pinning the whole contract from v1.46.0 to v1.48.0 also brings in 1.46.x-1.47.0 changes unrelated to A2UI. A2UI-D8 decides between a full re-pin and a scoped addition recorded in SDK_ADDITIONS.md.

docs.title: 5. Attributes
docs.text:
All names are a2ui.* additions of this library and are marked provisional: there is no OpenTelemetry convention for A2UI. Multi-valued rules follow 1.47.0's A2A rules: a single-valued identifier is omitted when one operation saw several distinct values, and lists are sorted and de-duplicated.

Always recorded. These are identifiers, counts and codes, not content:

Attribute Meaning a2ui.protocol.version 1.0, 0.9, 0.8 (single value; omitted if mixed) a2ui.agent_message.count Agent-to-renderer messages in the operation a2ui.renderer_message.count Renderer-to-agent messages in the operation a2ui.message.types Sorted distinct message types, snake_case (create_surface, update_components, action, error, ...) a2ui.surface.id / a2ui.surface.count The surface, when single; the distinct surface count a2ui.catalog.id / a2ui.catalog.ids The catalog when single; all catalogs referenced a2ui.component.count Components in updateComponents messages a2ui.renderer.supported_catalog_ids From the renderer capabilities metadata a2ui.action.name The user action's name, when single (see A2UI-D3) a2ui.function.name For callAgentFunction / callRendererFunction, when single a2ui.error.codes / a2ui.error.count Renderer and function error codes; their count a2ui.validation.outcome valid / invalid (agent-side parsing, section 3.2) a2ui.extension.active The A2A extension URI was negotiated

Recorded only with content capture on:

  • a2ui.messages, the JSON of the messages, truncated at the existing content limit;
  • the data-model values in updateDataModel;
  • the action's context;
  • the error path and message, because a validation message can quote user data;
  • the component type names (see A2UI-D3).

Never recorded: the content of image or file URLs inside components.

Span status.

  • A renderer error message or a function error does not by itself make the A2A span ERROR. The call carrying it succeeded; this follows A2A-D5. It sets a2ui.error.codes.
  • The agent-side a2ui.parse_response span is ERROR on a parse or validation failure, because that operation failed.
  • The Node a2ui.apply span is ERROR when the renderer rejected the batch.

Span events. One event a2ui.error per renderer error, with a2ui.error.code and a2ui.surface.id, so each error is visible even when one operation carries several.

docs.title: 6. Configuration
docs.text:
• GENAI_A2UI_ENABLED (default true) turns the A2UI attributes and spans off without touching A2A.
  • The instrumentor a2ui is added to DEFAULT_INSTRUMENTORS. It is a no-op without a2ui-agent-sdk. The A2A enrichment of section 3.1 lives in the a2a instrumentor and follows GENAI_A2UI_ENABLED.
  • The existing content-capture setting governs everything in section 5's second list. There is no separate A2UI capture switch.

docs.title: 7. Tests
docs.text:
No network and no real servers are used. The optional libraries are imported with importorskip, since CI installs only .[dev]; a2ui-agent-sdk is added to the dev extra.

  • Python.
  • A2A 1.x parts carrying A2UI in both shapes (one message per part, list per part), under both media types.
  • Request and response sides, and streaming.
  • parse_response valid and invalid, including an LLM span as parent.
  • open_stream totals.
  • process_message for action, callAgentFunction and error.
  • Content capture off and on.
  • Multi-value omission.
  • GENAI_A2UI_ENABLED=false.
  • No-op without the package.
  • v0.8 counted but not parsed.
  • Node.
  • @a2a-js/sdk client spans and trace injection.
  • A2UI parsing on request and response.
  • The public API under each entry point (Node, browser bundle, React Native bundle).
  • The web_core adapter against @a2ui/web_core 0.15.
  • Content rules.

docs.title: 8. Decisions for approval
docs.text: Question Recommendation A2UI-D1 Python: enrich A2A 1.x spans (3.1) and instrument a2ui-agent-sdk directly (3.2), so agents on A2A 0.3, ADK or MCP are covered Yes. The official A2UI-over-A2A bridge pins a2a-sdk 0.3, which our A2A instrumentor does not cover A2UI-D2 Do not extend the 1.47.0 A2A instrumentor to a2a-sdk 0.3 in this release Yes. The agent-SDK spans cover the A2UI signal; A2A 0.3 support is its own change if wanted A2UI-D3 Content rule: ids, counts, types of message, catalog ids, action and function names, error codes always; payloads, data-model values, action context, error path and message, and component type names only under content capture Yes. Action names are developer-defined identifiers, like span names. Component type names in a custom catalog can describe a business process, as skill names do (A2A-D4) A2UI-D4 A renderer error does not by itself make the carrying A2A span ERROR; an agent-side parse or validation failure does make its own span ERROR Yes A2UI-D5 Node: add A2A client instrumentation for @a2a-js/sdk as part of this work Yes. Without it a mobile or web app gets no A2UI telemetry and no trace from tap to agent A2UI-D6 Node: A2A server instrumentation (agents written in Node) Later. Apps are clients; Node agents can follow A2UI-D11 Node: instrument the TypeScript agent SDK @a2ui/agent (4.0), not only renderers Yes. It is the official agent SDK for Node and costs one wrapper on the same two methods as Python A2UI-D7 Node: renderer adapters. The @a2ui/web_core adapter now; React Native through the A2A path and the public API, with no adapter for a community renderer Yes. Revisit an a2ui-react-native-renderer adapter if a customer standardises on it A2UI-D8 Node contract: add the A2A and A2UI names as a scoped addition from the v1.48.0 tag (recorded in SDK_ADDITIONS.md and the parity matrix), not a full re-pin from v1.46.0 Scoped addition. A full re-pin pulls in unrelated 1.46.x-1.47.0 changes A2UI-D9 Go: not in this release. Go's A2UI libraries are community agent libraries at v0.9 and two terminal renderers, and the Go port has no A2A support yet Later, as a separate spec covering A2A and A2UI for Go together A2UI-D10 Versions: Python ships as 1.48.0, so the parked price-identity release moves to the next minor. The Node work ships as the next npm alpha of the Node port (corrected 2026-11-12: it is published on npm) Yes

docs.title: 9. Out of scope
docs.text:
• Flutter, SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose renderers. They need Dart, Swift and Kotlin instrumentation, and this library has no Dart or Swift port.
  • Metrics. Spans only, as with A2A.
  • Rendering performance beyond the web_core adapter's batch duration (frame timing, layout).
  • Proposing A2UI conventions upstream to OpenTelemetry. This is worth doing once the attributes have been used.

docs.title: 10. Implementation notes and deviations (1.48.0)
docs.text:
The Python part (sections 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7-Python; A2UI-D1 to D4 and D10) as built. Checked against a2ui-agent-sdk 0.11.0 and a2ui-core 0.6.0 as installed, and a2a-sdk 1.3.0. The Node part is not in this change.

Layout: genai_otel/a2ui_semconv/ holds attributes.py (names, media types, constants), extract.py (the shared reader, an A2uiObservation over wire-format dicts; it imports neither a2a nor a2ui) and instrumentor.py (A2UIInstrumentor, the agent-SDK wrappers). The A2A path adds an optional a2ui accumulator to a2a_semconv.extract.Observation, shared by a call's request and response, so a single-valued key seen as two values across the two sides is omitted.

Signatures checked against the installed package, and wrapped as follows:

  • A2uiRequestProcessor.parse_response(self, content, wrapped=True, *, state=None) returns list[ResponsePart]; A2uiPart.a2ui is a list of pydantic schema models, read through model_dump(mode="json", by_alias=True, exclude_unset=True) with the model's version put back (a v1.0 model leaves version unset, so a plain dump drops it).
  • A2uiRequestProcessor.open_stream(self, *, wrapped=True, state=None, after_rejected_block="end") is synchronous and returns a ResponseStream whose feed(chunk) and close() are synchronous. The span starts in open_stream (a child of the current span, but not made current, because it outlives the call) and ends when close() returns or feed / close raises. The two methods are replaced on the stream instance. A stream that is never closed ends its span when it is garbage collected.
  • RendererToAgentMessageProcessor.process_message(self, message) is async and returns ProcessResult(handled, replies). Its replies go back to the renderer, so they are counted as agent messages.

Deviations and choices the spec left open:

  1. parse_content_to_parts lives in a2ui-a2a, not in a2ui-agent-sdk. a2ui/a2a/parts.py imports a2a.types.DataPart, which a2a-sdk 1.x does not have, so it cannot be imported beside the 1.x the A2A tests need. It is wrapped only when a2ui.a2a.parts imports. Because the function swallows the exception inside itself, the wrapper cannot see it; it notices the Failed to parse A2UI response: <class> warning the function logs (a log filter that only reads, installed on the a2ui.a2a.parts logger and keyed to a context variable that is set only while the wrapper runs). Nothing is suppressed or changed. Consequence: it is missed if that logger is set above WARNING. The failure is recorded as a2ui.validation.outcome=invalid on the current span plus an event a2ui.validation_failed carrying error.type; error.type is not set as an attribute and the span is not made ERROR, because the operation did not fail. Not verified against the real module, only against a stand-in with the same name, logger and message, taken from the 0.3.0 source.
  2. Rejected block in a continuing stream. A stream opened with after_rejected_block="continue" returns an ErrorPart instead of raising. a2ui.parse_stream is ERROR for it too (a block failed validation), with error.type set to the error's class and the outcome invalid.
  3. a2ui.process only sets invalid on a validation exception. The SDK does not validate a message that has no callback, so a successful call does not claim valid. An unrecognised message names its span a2ui.process unknown.
  4. a2ui.component.count also counts createSurface.components. The v1.0 schema lets createSurface carry components, so counting only updateComponents would undercount.
  5. Extension and header names. a2a-sdk 1.x renamed the header to A2A-Extensions; the spec text says X-A2A-Extensions. Both names are read, from the client's service_parameters, the server's requested_extensions and request headers, and Message.extensions / Artifact.extensions. Any URI under https://a2ui.org/a2a-extension/a2ui/ matches, so a v0.8 or v0.9 extension URI also sets a2ui.extension.active. The attribute is written only when true.
  6. Content attribute names the spec left open (provisional, a2ui.*): a2ui.messages, a2ui.data_model, a2ui.action.context (JSON strings), a2ui.error.paths, a2ui.error.messages, a2ui.component.types (string lists). Each is dropped with content capture off, and nothing of the payload is held in memory then. The event a2ui.validation_failed is the one event name beyond a2ui.error.
  7. Media URLs are scrubbed. Inside the components of createSurface / updateComponents, the value of a key named url, src, uri or ending in Url / Uri becomes [redacted] (a {"@path": ...} binding is kept, since it names where a value lives); a string starting data: is redacted anywhere. The existing a2a.*.data content attribute is also written from the scrubbed copy for A2UI parts, but only when the A2UI reader is on; with GENAI_A2UI_ENABLED=false that attribute is exactly what 1.47.0 wrote.
  8. v0.8 is detected by the missing version field, counted, and its content is not recorded. Versions are normalised to major.minor (v0.9.1 is 0.9).
  9. a2ui.renderer.supported_catalog_ids is the union over the per-version map, and over either metadata key, and over message.metadata and SendMessageRequest.metadata.
  10. Packaging and tests. genai_otel.a2ui_semconv is in [tool.setuptools] packages. a2ui-agent-sdk>=0.11,<1 is in the dev extra; a2ui-a2a is deliberately not (it would downgrade a2a-sdk). There is no optional extra for A2A, so none was added for A2UI. The tests importorskip the SDK and use the real processors; the A2A path runs over the same in-process ASGI rig as the A2A tests.

Not verified: the real a2ui.a2a.parts module (see 1); a2ui-agent-sdk versions other than 0.11.0; the A2UI extension header on gRPC; Google ADK and MCP transports (the wrappers are transport-independent, and are tested only through the processors).

docs.title: Gemini Decisions API instrumentation (spec)
docs.text: Status: APPROVED 2026-11-12. GD-D1 to GD-D5 are approved as recommended. It ships in 1.47.0 together with the SeaweedFS change.

docs.title: 1. Problem
docs.text:
Google released the Gemini Decisions API on 2026-11-11, with the model gemini-decision-1. A decision call takes a shared input plus up to 1,000 named, typed questions, and returns a probability or a distribution for each one. It writes no text.

The library already emits DECISION spans (genai_otel/instrumentors/decision.py) for two wire protocols: OpenAI Decisions (POST /v1/decisions) and SystemOne (POST /v1/systemone). A Gemini decision call is not covered today:

  • google-genai's client.decisions.create is not wrapped. The Google instrumentor wraps only models.generate_content and the embeddings calls.
  • The plain-HTTP matcher (decision_http.py) recognises .../v1/decisions and .../v1/systemone. Gemini's REST path is POST https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/decisions. It does not match /v1/decisions, so a REST call gets no span, or only a generic HTTP span.
  • llm_pricing.json has no gemini-decision-1 entry, so cost is unpriced.

docs.title: 2. The API, as documented
docs.text:
Source: https://aistudio.google.com/docs/decisions-api (read 2026-11-11).

  • Request:
  • model;
  • input, which is a string, a Content, or a Content[]. Content blocks are text, image, audio, video and document, each carried as data or uri;
  • questions, a map from a name to {type, instructions, criteria?}.
  • Question types:
  • noul (yes/no, with optional true_description / false_description);
  • choice (criteria maps option keys to descriptions, 2-255 options);
  • score (criteria is an ordered list of levels, 2-255).
  • Response: answers is a map keyed by question name.
  • noul answers carry noul (0.01-0.99) and confidence.
  • choice answers carry choice, probabilities and confidence.
  • score answers carry score (the probability-weighted level index), legend, probabilities and confidence.
  • Usage:
  • total_input_tokens;
  • input_tokens_by_modality ([{modality, tokens}]);
  • total_output_tokens, which is always 0;
  • total_tokens.
  • Errors: HTTP 400 with error.code, which is one of safety, prohibited_content, blocklist, image_safety or content_blocked, and no answers. Limit violations also return 400. The API has no per-question refusal.
  • SDKs:
  • Python google-genai 3.2 or later: genai.Client(http_options={"api_version": "v1beta"}).decisions.create(...). An async variant is not documented.
  • JavaScript: ai.decisions.create(...).
  • Pricing: $0.10 per 1M input tokens and $0 for output. The shared input is billed once per request.

The shape is SystemOne's: a map of named questions (noul / choice / score) and a map of named answers. Only the usage block and the error shape differ.

docs.title: 3. Proposal
docs.text:
1. Protocol. Add PROTOCOL_GEMINI_DECISIONS = "gemini_decisions".
  2. Questions and answers are parsed by the existing SystemOne parsers (systemone_questions, systemone_answers), extended only where a field name differs. noul maps to the existing noul handling.
  3. A new gemini_usage reads total_input_tokens as input and total_output_tokens as output. When the response carries input_tokens_by_modality, the per-modality input counts are recorded as decision.token_count.input.<modality>. That is a new attribute; see D3.
  4. SDK path. The Google instrumentor wraps client.decisions.create, and the async variant when one exists, through the existing BaseDecisionInstrumentor and DecisionRecorder. One decision is one span, of kind DECISION.
  5. decision.system = "google", matching the instrumentor's gen_ai.system.
  6. decision.provider = "google".
  7. The operation is google.genai.decisions.
  8. The instrumentor stays a no-op when the installed google-genai has no decisions attribute (older than 3.2).
  9. GENAI_ENABLED_INSTRUMENTORS keeps its meaning: the Google instrumentor owns these calls, as the OpenAI instrumentor owns OpenAI decisions.
  10. REST path. decision_http.py matches POST to a path ending in /v1beta/decisions or /v1/decisions, only on host generativelanguage.googleapis.com. Those requests are parsed as gemini_decisions. An OpenAI-compatible server on any other host keeps today's behaviour.
  11. A request made from inside a decision span this library already opened is left alone, as today.
  12. generativelanguage.googleapis.com is added to the provider host map as google.
  13. Errors. A 400 with an error.code sets the span status to ERROR, with error.type = <error.code>. The span records no answers and no refusals, because the API has no per-question refusal. Question counts are still recorded from the request.
  14. Content. The existing rule is unchanged. With content capture off, the span records:
  15. which model, through which provider;
  16. how many questions, of which types;
  17. tokens and cost.

Chosen answers, probabilities, confidence and question names are recorded only with content capture on. Media in input is replaced by the existing placeholders. 6. Pricing. Add decision.gemini-decision-1 at $0.10/1M input and $0 output, citing the Google source. The chat table gets no entry, so the model is never priced as chat. 7. Tests. - SDK path: sync, plus async if it exists, using a fake client, so that no network and no google-genai install is needed (importorskip if real types are used). - REST path: requests and httpx. - Each of the three question types, with content capture both off and on. - The 400 safety error. - The inside_decision_span de-duplication. - The host gate: /v1beta/decisions on another host is not treated as Gemini. - The pricing lookup.

docs.title: 4. Decisions for approval
docs.text: Question Recommendation GD-D1 Reuse the SystemOne parsers under a new protocol id, rather than writing a separate parser Yes. The shape is the same GD-D2 REST matching only on generativelanguage.googleapis.com Yes. A path-only match would misread other servers' /v1beta/decisions GD-D3 Record the per-modality input tokens as a new decision.token_count.input.<modality> attribute Yes, behind content capture off. Counts are not content, and they explain cost on multimodal inputs GD-D4 A safety block is an ERROR span, not refusals Yes. The API returns no answers GD-D5 Ship together with the SeaweedFS change in one minor release Yes, per the founder's request

docs.title: 5. Out of scope
docs.text:
• Vertex AI (Gemini in Google Cloud). Google says support is "coming soon"; the gap is recorded here as a follow-up.
  • The JavaScript SDK. The Python library cannot see it.
  • Upstream semantic-convention proposals for the noul type.

docs.title: 6. Implementation notes
docs.text:
Implemented as specified. Details and deviations:

  • Usage reader. gemini_decision_usage (in decision.py) reads the Gemini block. usage_of delegates to it whenever the block carries total_input_tokens or total_output_tokens, so the base wrapper's cost and token metrics need no Gemini-specific hook. DecisionUsage gained input_tokens_by_modality (modality names lower-cased, enum values unwrapped).
  • Parsers. Answers go through systemone_answers unchanged (noul already maps to the predicate type); no parser change was needed.
  • Error code on the SDK path. The API's error.code is read from the exception's details (or response_json) when it is a name, not an HTTP number. error.type is set only then. An exception with no named code keeps the base wrapper's ERROR status without error.type (the spec did not say what to record, and inventing a value would misreport the cause).
  • Error code on the REST path. Same rule; when the 400 body carries no named code, error.type falls back to the HTTP status string, as for every other decision protocol.
  • Host gate. On generativelanguage.googleapis.com only /v1beta/decisions and /v1/decisions match, and both are Gemini. Any other path on that host matches nothing.
  • Async. client.aio.decisions.create is wrapped only when present, through the same tracer (span name google.genai.aio.decisions). Verified with a fake client; not against a real SDK, because an async variant is undocumented.
  • Provider. decision.provider is fixed to google on the SDK path (the SDK's base URL is not read); the REST path derives it from the host map.
  • Not verified against a real google-genai install. The tests use fakes shaped like the documented response (answers as a map of attribute-access objects).

docs.title: SeaweedFS instrumentation (spec)
docs.text:
Status: APPROVED 2026-11-11 (implemented in the Unreleased changes).

Approved decisions:

  • D1: keep db.system="s3"; add db.system.name="seaweedfs" only on declared endpoints; always emit server.port; add aws.s3.bucket / aws.s3.key alongside the legacy s3.bucket / s3.object (legacy names are deprecated but not removed in a patch).
  • D2: use the custom seaweedfs value now. Follow-up: propose an upstream well-known value.
  • D3: declared endpoints only (GENAI_OTEL_SEAWEEDFS_ENDPOINTS, auto-filled from the seaweed media-store endpoint); no port heuristic.
  • D4: the SDK's own media-store spans are suppressed by default via OpenTelemetry's standard suppression context; GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_STORE_TRACE_CALLS=true opts back in.
  • D5: conservative path. requests is NOT patched. The Filer is covered through httpx and aiohttp only, for declared Filer hosts.

Implementation notes and deviations from the draft below:

  • Filer spans are made by wrapping httpx.Client / AsyncClient._send_single_request and aiohttp.ClientSession._request. If the generic httpx instrumentation is also enabled, the generic client span and the Filer span are siblings; the Filer span is the one that carries the SeaweedFS meaning. De-duplication is a follow-up.
  • Open follow-ups: requests support for the Filer (needs a proof that OTLP exporters are unaffected); upstream semconv proposal for a SeaweedFS / object-store db.system.name; confirm response headers on a live gateway and Filer (Q3); an aiohttp trace-config variant.

docs.title: 1. Problem
docs.text:
Today SeaweedFS is observable only through its S3 gateway, via the botocore patch in genai_otel/mcp_instrumentors/s3_instrumentor.py:

  • every span carries db.system="s3", the same as AWS S3 and MinIO;
  • server.address is the hostname only (by design, to keep credentials and paths out), so there is no port and SeaweedFS cannot be told apart from AWS;
  • the Filer HTTP API (the path SeaweedFS-native clients use) has no instrumentation;
  • async S3 clients are not covered (section 4);
  • the SDK's own media-store uploads produce s3.* spans, which is noise in user traces (section 5).

docs.title: 2.1 What was verified (upstream docs and source, master branch)
docs.text:
Fact Evidence S3 gateway default port is 8333 weed/command/s3.go: -port default 8333 Filer default port is 8888 weed/command/filer.go: -port default 8888 The gateway sets x-amz-request-id only when the response lacks one weed/util/request_id middleware No Server header or X-Seaweedfs-* response header was found in s3api_server.go or the filer command file source read; not an exhaustive audit of every handler The Filer sets Seaweed-* response headers only for user tags Filer Server API wiki

Conclusion: response headers cannot identify SeaweedFS. x-amz-request-id is also what AWS sends, and no vendor header was found. Detection therefore rests on configuration, with the port as a weak hint. Before implementation, re-check a live gateway with curl -i (open question Q3), because docs and source reading are not proof of runtime behaviour.

docs.title: 2.2 Semantic-convention position
docs.text:
• server.port is a standard attribute. It is always emitted (when the endpoint states or implies one), regardless of vendor.
  • db.system is deprecated upstream in favour of db.system.name. The registry has no well-known value for S3, object stores or SeaweedFS (only aws.dynamodb, aws.redshift among AWS ones), and says a custom value MAY be used.
  • The AWS S3 attributes are aws.s3.bucket, aws.s3.key (Development status), alongside rpc.method and aws.request_id. The current instrumentor emits non-standard s3.bucket / s3.object instead.

docs.title: 2.3 Proposal
docs.text:
1. Always add server.port to S3 spans.
  2. Add aws.s3.bucket and aws.s3.key next to the existing s3.bucket / s3.object (keep the old ones for one minor version, mark deprecated in the changelog), and aws.request_id from the x-amz-request-id response header when present.
  3. When the endpoint matches a declared SeaweedFS endpoint (2.4), add db.system.name="seaweedfs". On all other S3 spans add nothing new, so existing dashboards keyed on db.system="s3" keep working.
  4. Keep db.system="s3" unchanged on gateway spans (it names the API dialect in use); see decision D1.

docs.title: 2.4 Detection by configuration
docs.text:
New setting GENAI_OTEL_SEAWEEDFS_ENDPOINTS: comma-separated host:port entries (the gateway and the Filer may both be listed). Matching is exact on lowercased host and port, after resolving the default port of the scheme. An optional wildcard host (*.internal) is allowed; no regexes.

Convenience: if GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_STORE=seaweed, its endpoint is added to the declared set automatically, so the SDK's own uploads are labelled with no extra setup.

No automatic classification by port number alone. A port heuristic (8333 / 8888) is rejected as a default because 8888 is also Jupyter's port and 8333 is Bitcoin's; it may be offered as an explicit opt-in (D3).

docs.title: 3.1 Scope
docs.text:
A lightweight instrumentor named SeaweedFilerInstrumentor, enabled by GENAI_ENABLE_SEAWEEDFS_INSTRUMENTATION (default true, but inert unless at least one endpoint is declared; with none declared it does nothing and costs nothing).

It must work with the clients applications really use. Filer clients are plain HTTP, so the real surface is:

Client Status today Plan httpx Patched by HTTPXClientInstrumentor only when enable_http_instrumentation is on (default off) Hook at the httpx transport level, independent of that flag requests Deliberately NOT instrumented (manager.py: patching requests.Session breaks OTLP HTTP exporters) Wrap Session.send narrowly, applying only to declared Filer hosts, so the exporter (different host) is never touched. Needs a test proving an OTLP exporter on another host is unaffected. See Q2 aiohttp Not covered Same pattern, via a trace config on ClientSession creation; optional, phase 2 pyseaweed (PyPI, 2.0.0) Not verified; it appears to target the master/volume servers, not the Filer, and its HTTP library and maintenance status were not confirmed Out of scope unless Q1 shows it is used

No other Python Filer SDK was found on PyPI under the obvious names (seaweedfs, seaweed-client, seaweedfs-client, weed-python all absent). Because everything is plain HTTP, a transport-level hook with host matching covers any wrapper library for free.

docs.title: 3.2 Span shape
docs.text:
• Name: seaweedfs.filer.<operation>.
  • Kind: CLIENT.
  • Operations, derived from method plus query string (documented Filer API): upload (POST/PUT), append (op=append), download (GET/HEAD on a path), list (GET with a trailing slash or JSON accept), stat (?metadata), delete, delete_recursive, move (mv.from), copy (cp.from), mkdir, tag (?tagging), else other.
  • Attributes:
  • db.system.name="seaweedfs", db.operation.name=<operation>
  • server.address, server.port, http.request.method, http.response.status_code
  • url.path.prefix: first N path segments only (default 2), never the full path; query strings are never recorded
  • seaweedfs.request.size from Content-Length of the request, and seaweedfs.response.size from the response Content-Length, when stated
  • error.type on failure: exception class name or the status code, never error text
  • Never recorded: file contents, filenames beyond the prefix, query values (they can carry Seaweed-* tag values), headers, credentials.
  • Status: 5xx and transport errors are ERROR; 4xx are ERROR except 404 on stat/download, which is unset (an absent file is an answer, not a fault).
  • Streaming bodies are never read or buffered by the instrumentor.

docs.title: 3.3 Interaction with the HTTP instrumentor
docs.text: If httpx instrumentation is also on, a Filer call would produce two spans. The Filer instrumentor must suppress or parent itself to avoid duplicates (decision: it replaces the generic HTTP client span for declared Filer hosts). Test required.

docs.title: 4. Async S3 clients
docs.text:
Client Call path Covered today Plan boto3 / botocore (sync) botocore.client.BaseClient._make_api_call Yes keep aiobotocore AioBaseClient(BaseClient) overrides _make_api_call as async def (verified in upstream source) No: the override replaces the patched method, so no span is produced Add an async wrapper on AioBaseClient._make_api_call, sharing attribute logic with the sync path aioboto3 Thin wrapper over aiobotocore No (same reason) Covered by the aiobotocore wrapper s3fs Uses aiobotocore; a filesystem call fans out to several S3 operations No Covered by the aiobotocore wrapper; add a parent span only if Q4 says users want one s3fs.* span per file operation

Requirements: the wrapper must be a coroutine that awaits the original, record the same attributes and the same error handling (type only, no message), be removable by uninstrument(), and be skipped silently when aiobotocore is not installed. Tests need a fake AioBaseClient, not a network.

docs.title: 5. Suppressing the SDK's own media-store calls (optional)
docs.text:
The media-store fix (1.46.8 candidate) bounds the cost of an unreachable store, but a failed or successful upload still emits s3.* spans into the user's trace.

Proposal: wrap the S3 media store's boto calls (create_bucket, put_object) in OpenTelemetry's standard suppression context (opentelemetry.context _SUPPRESS_INSTRUMENTATION_KEY set via attach / detach), and make the S3 instrumentor honour it by returning the original call when the key is set. The key is OTel's own mechanism but its constant is in a private-named module attribute; pin the import behind a small shim with a test that fails if it moves.

Setting: GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_STORE_TRACE_CALLS (default false, i.e. suppress). Setting it to true keeps today's nested spans, which the multimodal guide currently documents, so that page needs updating either way. This is a behaviour change, hence D4.

docs.title: 6. Configuration
docs.text:
Name Default Meaning GENAI_ENABLE_SEAWEEDFS_INSTRUMENTATION true Filer instrumentor; inert without endpoints GENAI_OTEL_SEAWEEDFS_ENDPOINTS empty Declared gateway/Filer host:port list GENAI_OTEL_SEAWEEDFS_PATH_PREFIX_SEGMENTS 2 Path segments kept in url.path.prefix GENAI_OTEL_MEDIA_STORE_TRACE_CALLS false Keep spans for the SDK's own uploads

Naming follows the existing split: GENAI_ENABLE_* for feature toggles, GENAI_OTEL_* for the media/storage settings. Each gets a field on OTelConfig.

docs.title: 7. Tests
docs.text:
• Unit, no network: operation derivation table (every Filer verb and query form); path prefix truncation and query stripping; 404 handling; endpoint matching (exact, default ports, wildcard, non-match); server.port present on S3 spans.
  • Privacy: assert no body bytes, query values, full paths, credentials or error text appear on any span (extend the existing S3 privacy tests).
  • Duplicate-span test with httpx instrumentation on.
  • OTLP-exporter non-interference test for the requests wrapper.
  • aiobotocore: fake async client, success, error, uninstrument, aiobotocore absent.
  • Suppression: media upload produces no s3.* span by default and does with TRACE_CALLS=true; unrelated user S3 calls are still traced in the same context.
  • Back-compat: db.system="s3" still present; old s3.bucket / s3.object still present.

docs.title: 8. Documentation plan
docs.text:
• New guide docs/guides/seaweedfs.md (add to mkdocs.yml nav) with endpoints setup, span reference and a Jaeger/Grafana filter example.
  • Update docs/guides/multimodal.md (nested-span sentence), docs/reference/semantic-conventions.md (new attributes, deprecations), docs/getting-started/configuration.md (env table), README.md storage line.
  • CHANGELOG entries under Added / Changed / Deprecated.

docs.title: 9. Decisions for the founder
docs.text:
• D1. Keep db.system="s3" and add db.system.name="seaweedfs" only on matched endpoints (recommended, non-breaking), or switch matched spans to db.system="seaweedfs"?
  • D2. Is a custom seaweedfs value acceptable given the registry has none, or should we propose one upstream?
  • D3. Offer an explicit opt-in port heuristic (8333/8888), or require declared endpoints only?
  • D4. Suppress the SDK's own media-store spans by default (recommended), accepting a visible behaviour change from the documented nested spans?
  • D5. Approve wrapping requests.Session.send for declared Filer hosts only, given the history of exporter breakage (Q2)?

docs.title: 10. Open questions
docs.text:
• Q1. Which Filer clients do target users actually run (requests, httpx, aiohttp, a FUSE mount, pyseaweed)? FUSE mounts and the Go/Java clients are invisible to this SDK.
  • Q2. Can the requests wrapper be proven safe for OTLP exporters, or should Filer support ship httpx/aiohttp only first?
  • Q3. Confirm on a running gateway and Filer which response headers are actually set; source reading found none useful.
  • Q4. Should s3fs get a parent span per filesystem operation, or are per-S3-call spans enough?
  • Q5. Does the gateway honour x-amz-request-id per request, so aws.request_id is usable for correlation with gateway logs?
